One industry that has been growing at a rapid pace in recent years is wineries, and more specifically that of the wine bar.
Today, we wanted to share some of our favorites from our explorations around the city!
### 🏨 **Book a Hotel in Pittsburgh**
  1. **Great Value:** Drury Plaza offers excellent prices downtown.
  2. **Good Views:** Sheraton Station Square features stellar views from river-view rooms.
  3. **Free Parking:** Hampton Inn Strip District includes free parking and a great location.


🏡 Looking for an apartment rental? Find a deal on Airbnb!
## **Not Everything Can Be a Pittsburgh Wine Bar**
Unlike other articles of this nature, such as our goal in finding the best Pittsburgh breweries, we have to take a step back and answer one very important question up-front: **what is the difference between a wine bar and a winery?**
To us, the main distinction is based on where the wine is made. A winery makes their own wine and serves it on-property (and we have many Pittsburgh wineries to check out) while wine bars are just that- _a_ _bar._
There are a few wineries that blur the line and make this list because they feel more like bars than wineries, despite the fact that they make their own wines. 
But for the most part, a wine bar (in how we look at it at least) is simply an awesome bar that has a stellar wine list- be it of their own creations or from others.
This guide features some of the best wine bars in Pittsburgh that we have had the luxury of visiting in our exploration of the city.
## **Allegheny Wine Mixer**
Allegheny Wine Mixer in Lawrenceville may be our idea of the perfect wine bar.
**Why is that?** This intimate bar is beautifully decorated, offers a superb wine list, reasonable prices, rotating special features, and a modest beer and cocktail list for non-wine drinkers as well!
While you may never know what you’re going to get when visiting this one, you are guaranteed to have a good time all the same.
_Allegheny Wine Mixer is located at 5326 Butler Street in Lawrenceville._
## **Solera Wine Co**
Solera Wine Co is a second wine bar located in the heart of Lawrenceville and is one part bar and one part bottle shop with wines that can be enjoyed both on-site and to go.
This one offers a bright and welcoming ambiance complete with a small plates food menu, modest cocktail selections, and more- making it a great option for a pre-dinner drink, after dinner digestif, or for a night out on its own! 
_Solera Wine Co is located at 4839 Butler Street in Lawrenceville._ /div>
## **Apericena Wine Bar**
Apericena Wine Bar is a high-end wine bar in Pittsburgh’s South Hills that offers glasses and flights of an array of obscure and award-winning wines (be sure to check the menu for critically rated bottles!).
While only about half of the menu is available by the glass, the large selection ensures there is always something new to try. But as far as wine bars go, this one comes in among the highest priced in this list. 
Start with a flight and see where the spirits take you!
_Apericena Wine Bar is located at 100 Sienna Drive in Upper St. Clair, just next toThe Porch and across from South Hills Village._
## **Eighth & Hays**
In a way, Eighth & Hays is a bit of a hybrid between Apericena and Allegheny Wine Mixer above. 
The ambiance of this bar is formal and the wines include affordable house wines and hand-picked, high-end offerings that you can typically only get by-the-bottle elsewhere.
But what makes this wine bar different is that you can order  _any wine_ in one, three, or full six ounce pours in addition to purchasing by the bottle. The prices are reflected in the quality of the wines, naturally, but there is something to be said about being able to try a half-glass of a high-end bottle that we just absolutely love.
**Where else can you do that?**
_Eighth & Hays is located at 130 W 8th Avenue in Homestead._
## **Lorelei**
We’ll be the first to admit that we often find ourselves visiting Lorelei for their cocktail bar and German beer program (not to mention the awesome ambiance). But we’d be remiss if we did not include this specialty bar in our wine bar list as well.
Why? Their wine list is one of the most impressive we’ve seen when it comes to European wines (namely wines from France, Germany, Austria, and Italy).
Can’t decide on what to order? Give a themed flight a try as well. There is always room for a Riesling flight here! 
_Lorelei is located at 124 South Highland Avenue in East Liberty._
## **The Pennsylvania Market**
In the Strip District, one of the finest wine bars is located in the second-floor dining room of The Pennsylvania Market on 19th Street. Tucked away in a quiet corner is their aptly named Wine Library which features 150 different grape varietals that are available to purchase with a selection by the glass, by the bottle, or via a flight. 
So while you can visit this one for a glass, you can also walk out with some bottles you may not otherwise be able to find at the state store.
During my visit, their wine list had a healthy spread of conventionally known grapes and a few lesser-known but still tasty varietals which made for a great way to taste your way around the menu be it white, red, or rose in a relaxing setting. That being said, as these wines are starting to shift to premium levels, be prepared for a price to match (for some at least)!
_Pennsylvania Market is located at 108 19th St in the Strip District._
## **Spill Wine Bar**
If a cozy wine bar with a handpicked menu is more your speed, to check out Spill Wine Bar which opened in early 2019.
The wine bar is quite similar in that it is an intimate space and they serve only four vineyards (three from Italy, including Collefrisio, as well as one from Australia) and have an exceptional selection from each. 
You can visit this one for a tasting full of complimentary offerings to find your preferred bottles (the samples really kept on coming for us), or purchase glasses at competitive prices. No matter what you’ll do you will sample some great wines, have some wonderful conversation with the friendly owners, and likely be walking out with a few bottles all while planning a return visit- we did!
_Spill Wine Bar is located at 4800 Liberty Avenue in Bloomfield._
## **Whisper**
Whisper in the Cultural District brands itself as a high-end wine and dessert bar, and has an impressive lineup of premium bottles of wines from brands you may know (and a killer dessert menu to go along with it). While we wish this one had more dessert wines to go along with the killer dessert menu, for those who want a nice glass of wine downtown, this one is a great option.
_Whisper is located at 932 Penn Avenue in the Cultural District._
## **Barcelona Wine Bar**
Barcelona Wine Bar is a second wine bar in the Cultural District and is a local branch of the popular national chain known for Spanish wines (and wines from Spanish speaking countries), tapas, and more.
One of the best things about Barcelona Wine Bar’s wine menu is that they have one of the largest by-the-glass menus in the city, and most all of the wines are also available as a half pour- giving you an opportunity to easily taste your way around the menu with DIY flights!
_Barcelona Wine Bar is located at 922 Penn Avenue in the Cultural District._
## **Refucilo Winery**
In a way, Refucilo Winery is a lot like a few other wine bars on this list that carry a limited but highly curated selection of wines.
This one is an Argentinian based winery whose owners live in the Pittsburgh area and decided to open a tasting room to share their delicious Malbec, Torrontes, and other South American creations with the region. 
A specialty wine bar, yes, but superb products that will keep you coming back for more as well.
A nice little gem in the North Side!
_Refucilo is located at 907 Western Avenue in the North Side._
## **EngineHouse 25**
EngineHouse 25 is located just a mile or so away at the boundary of the Strip District and Lawrenceville and comes packed with a wonderful ambiance, delicious wines made with grapes imported from around the world, and an incredible backstory.
Plan your visit around a tour of the Clemente Museum (attached to the winery- reservations required) for a great day out. If you are just visiting for wine, reservations are not needed!
_EngineHouse 25 is located at 3339 Penn Avenue in Lawrenceville._
## **Honorable Mention – Palate Partners Wine Classes**
We’ll be the first to admit that Palate Partners is not a wine bar in the traditional sense. To put it simply, they are not a regularly operating bar at all.
This one is a wine business that focuses on private and public wine classes in Pittsburgh– which we think is close enough! 
The reason why love this one so much (and why we want to give them an honorary placement on this list) is that they offer cheap, public wine tastings on the first and third Fridays of the month- offering six generous samples of curated wines for just $15.
No wine bar in the city can beat that, and their price to buy by the bottle is unmatched as well! If you want to build your wine cellar, this is the place to be.
_Palate Partners is located at 3401 Liberty Avenue in Lawrenceville._
**Know of another wine bar we have not visited yet?** Comment below to let us know about it!

We are lucky enough to have so much going on in the local sports scene that not a week goes by without a professional game of some sort. Throw on regional and local teams, and you have the opportunity to get out and enjoy a sporting event seemingly whenever you’d like.
In this one, we thought we’d take a look at all of the sports teams you would want to check out in the city, from the famous teams in the biggest leagues to minor leagues, colleges, and the independent groups you can join for a pickup game. 
So if you’re looking to enjoy sports in Pittsburgh, we’ve got you covered here!
**Note** : Our local colleges have dozens upon dozens of organized sports teams. We are only listing some that the universities and colleges are most well-known for in this one.
### 🏨 **Book a Hotel in Pittsburgh**
  1. **Great Value:** Drury Plaza offers excellent prices downtown.
  2. **Good Views:** Sheraton Station Square features stellar views from river-view rooms.
  3. **Free Parking:** Hampton Inn Strip District includes free parking and a great location.


🏡 Looking for an apartment rental? Find a deal on Airbnb!
## **Football**
Is there anything better than Steelers season in Pittsburgh? Well, there is far more than this popular NFL team to enjoy in the world of football!
  * **Pittsburgh Steelers** – The city’s resident NFL team playing home games at Acrisure Stadium on the North Shore. Regular season typically runs from September to January. 
    * For more great Steelers experiences, be sure to check out Training Camp in Latrobe.
  * **Pittsburgh Passion** – All-female football team in the WFA league playing games in Imperial, PA. Regular season typically runs April to June.
  * **Pitt Panthers** – The University of Pittsburgh’s NCAA Division I football team playing home games at Acrisure Stadium. Regular season typically runs August to November.


## **Hockey**
It’s a hockey night in Pittsburgh! We always love cheering on the Penguins on their quest for another Stanley Cup!
  * **Pittsburgh Penguins** – The city’s professional hockey team playing games at PPG Paints Arena in Uptown. Regular season typically runs October to April. 
    * For more great Penguins experiences, be sure to check out their public practices at the Mario Lemieux Complex!


## **Baseball**
Baseball is one of the city’s most popular sports, and between the Pirates, the Washington Wild Things, and college sports, there are many games to check out!
  * **Pittsburgh Pirates** – The city’s MLB team playing frequent games at PNC Park on the North Shore. Regular season typically runs March to September. 
    * If you love PNC Park like the rest of us, be sure to take a behind-the-scenes park tour!
  * **Washington Wild Things** – Frontier League baseball team playing home games at Wild Things Park in Washington, PA. Regular season typically runs May to August.
  * **Pitt Panthers Baseball **– Univeristy of Pittsburgh’s ACC baseball team playing home games at the Petersen Sports Complex. Regular season typically runs February to May.


## **Soccer**
Soccer is growing in popularity in Pittsburgh in recent years, and there are many great opportunities to check out this classic sport in the city.
  * **Pittsburgh Riverhounds** – USL Championship league soccer at Highmark Stadium in South Side. Regular season typically runs March to October.
  * **Pittsburgh Riveters **– All-female soccer team in the USL W league playing games at Highmark Stadium. First season expected in 2025.
  * **Steel City FC Men’s and Women’s** – Soccer club with youth to adult services in both men’s and women’s leagues. First teams typically play at Founders Field from April to July.


## **Basketball**
Although Pittsburgh doesn’t have a professional basketball team in the NBA, we have numerous organizations, particularly colleges, thriving in the basketball scene!
  * **Pitt Panthers** – University of Pittsburgh’s resident basketball team, which plays home games at the Petersen Event Center in Oakland. Regular season typically runs October to March.
  * **Duquesne Dukes** – Duquense’s resident A10 basketball team, playing home games at the UPMC Cooper Fieldhouse. Regular season typically runs October to March.
  * **Robert Morris Colonials** – RMU’s resident basketball team, playing home games at UPMC Events Center in Moon Township. Regular season typically runs October to March. 
  * **Steel City Yellowjackets** – Pittsburgh’s resident ABA basketball team. Regular season typically runs November to March.
  * **Steel City Queens** – Pittsburgh’s women ABA basketball team. Regular season typically runs July to August.


## **Other Sports**
Many other sports are represented in Pittsburgh, either via games you can watch or other leagues to join and participate, including the roller derby, dodgeball, and so much more!
  * **Pittsburgh Roller Derby** – A local roller derby league with teams like the Undead, Zom-Bees, and Ghouls.
  * **Three Rivers Dodgeball **– Pittsburgh’s resident dodgeball club, typically playing games on Wednesdays throughout the city.
  * **Pittsburgh Curling Club **– Our local curling club playing on Olympic style rinks in McKees Rocks. Watch out for their Learn to Curl classes for the public!
  * **Pittsburgh Thunderbirds Ultimate Frisbee **– The city’s resident UFA ultimate frisbee team, playing home games at Highmark Stadium. Regular season typically runs May to July.
  * **Steelwheelers** – A local organization for wheelchair users for rugby, basketball, and handcycling.
  * **Pittsburgh Harlequins **– A local rugby team that plays at Founders Field, typically from August to October.


**Do you know of an organized group for sports in Pittsburgh?** Comment below to let us know about it so we can add to this guide!

BACKSTORY
  

About
Pittsburgh Hall of Fame™ is home to The History of Sports in Pittsburgh!™ Here, you will find the world’s broadest collection of the uniforms and symbols worn by Pittsburgh’s teams over the years. Included are artifacts from nearly every style of jersey, helmet, and hat ever worn by the Steelers, Pirates, Penguins, and Pitt, together with classic souvenirs, collectibles and fan apparel. Vintage promotional and advertising items will bring the memories flooding back. The Hornets, Pipers, Condors, Spirit, original Maulers and more spring back to life through buried treasures that must be seen to be believed. Old game programs, souvenirs, and other historic items further document Pittsburgh’s great history of fielding the world’s best, and the world’s best-dressed, sports teams and fans. They also remember the city’s great moments. Even more importantly, our exhibits together with our  "Wall of Fame™" honor Pittsburgh’s greats and Pittsburgh’s great people. Our goal, with each and every "brick in the wall" is to honor and remember as many good, great, memorable, or perhaps even just likable, Pittsburgh players, coaches, athletes, and personalities from the “good old days” as possible, paired together with an original and unique memorabilia item. It is OUR great honor, just to be able to honor these great people! You may notice a particular emphasis on the two decades from 1972 to 1992. Well, that’s no coincidence as that’s when we grew up, and what a time it was to be a kid in Pittsburgh! We honor the modern greats as well, though we must admit it's a bit harder to get in the more recent the career. However, we are constantly adding enshrinees, and just because someone is not yet in does not mean they are not a Pittsburgh Hall-of-Famer™, it may be just a matter of time before yet  "Another Brick in the Hall™" is added to honor them! The city of Pittsburgh has been winning Championships since 1909, and even when the teams haven't been great, they have always (well, almost always) looked great! Pittsburgh itself is a living Hall of Fame and Museum and in the end that’s what Pittsburgh Hall of Fame™ is all about!
If you don't like it, you must be from Cleveland!™ Seriously though we really hope you do like it, and thank you very much for visiting!
Back to Top
Museum Exhibits
The museum exhibits have each been carefully selected to showcase a certain Pittsburgh look, uniform style, uniqueness, view, location, historic venue, etc., while commemorating great and memorable Pittsburgh moments, and remembering legendary players, coaches, and quintessentially-Pittsburgh personalities. To the best of our knowledge, each exhibit is an original item and not a reproduction, other than just a few exceptions which are noted. Every item is, again to the best of our knowledge, completely authentic, and exactly what we describe it as being, though this cannot be and is not guaranteed.  
  
The website is written from the perspective of our founder, "Uni", who is Pittsburgh born and raised. The stories and memories from growing up in the greatest city on Earth, experienced together with "Feamer," his best friend from third grade, and the rest of his childhood buddies, were his inspiration. This means there is a story to go with practically every exhibit! Stories from when they were kids, about the players they admired most, the games they went to (and they were many!), the sports and shows that they watched on tv, the stuff they collected and hung on their bedroom walls, the gear they wore to school, even Feamer's 3rd-grade lunchbox makes it in! You will never know which exhibit is going to bring out which particular story.  
  
We arrived at our conclusions for each exhibit, and what each one "is," through knowledge, research, memory (always dangerous, especially when you're trying to remember being 4 and 5 years old!), experience, logic, deduction, probability, and educated guesses. Ultimately, it is up to you to decide how each exhibit stacks up to the way we describe it! Did we make any mistakes (of course we did!)? Did we contridict ourselves somewhere (wouldn't surprise us!)? Are there any typos (a certainty!)? Or run-on sentences that you would like to condense (there are many!)? Do you have any additional information on a particular exhibit (which would be great!)? Do you have an item yourself that we don't, and you think it would fit in? If so,  please let us know! 
Back to Top
Hall of Fame Eligibility Categories
  

  1. Any Pittsburgh team member who has been elected to the Pro Football, Baseball, Hockey, Basketball, or College Football Hall of Fame.
  2. Any player on any Pittsburgh team who was involved in a memorable moment in time.
  3. Any player on any Pittsburgh team who we especially liked for one reason or another, or perhaps even no reason at all.
  4. Any member of a Pittsburgh championship-winning team. 
  5. Any non-sports related Pittsburgh celebrity or personality who we remember fondly.
  6. Any winner or top contender from a major individual sport championship event held in the Pittsburgh area.


None of the above categories guarantees enshrinement. Exhibit attribution in the museum, or inclusion in a photo, publication, roster, or other exhibit, does not by itself constitute enshrinement. The more recent the career, the more difficult enshrinement becomes. Criteria and rules are subject to change at our discretion at any time.
Do you want to nominate someone?  Send us a note here! 
##### NOT ELIGIBLE: Various goats (the lowercase kind) over the years, who shall not be named!
  

Back to Top
Backstory
Uni and Feamer, from whose perspectives  "Favorite Stories" are written, became best friends in third grade at recess on the first day of school when Uni, the new kid, asked to play quarterback and threw a perfect fly pattern TD pass to Feamer, who for the rest of the day kept saying “I can’t believe that pass!”, a story Feamer told years later as best man during the toast at Uni's wedding. But it was only with a Nerf, and that’s about when Uni peaked athletically. "Uni" is short for Univac, which was the name of an old IBM computer or something like that. Uni’s Dad used to call him Univac because he thought he was smart. It is true that Uni was unbeatable in “Streetcar”, a 3rd-grade math flashcard game where the streetcar is the kid who gets the flashcard challenge answer correct, and then moves on to the next kid’s desk for another round, and keeps going around the class until beaten. Alas, Uni also peaked academically in 3rd grade. Feamer is 3rd-grade for Femur, as in Femur bone, as in Feamer’s older brother said his femur bone stuck out when he ran. Despite his stature befitting the youngest person in the class, Feamer was an incredible athlete, and was the best soccer player at their late great elementary school. Feamer’s older brother played on the local high school's state-championship winning basketball team that year. Uni and Feamer created a map of a fictional land in 3rd-grade art class that commemorated their great season, and honored all of the players and coaches. Somewhere on that map you could visit Univac and Feamer Bar and Grill™, otherwise known as  . This red version of their "bar and grill" logo pays homage to that great team.

Pittsburgh is not known to be a wine capital in the US, let alone a highlight in the region, but that isn’t stopping local brewers and wine makers from producing some pretty incredible beverages. That is enough to get us excited, and we’re on a quest to find the gems that are worth your time.
When it comes to wineries in Pittsburgh, many go beyond the standard batch of fermented grapes to produce something completely unique. The following are some of the best that we have tried so far.
_Note:_ This guide also features cider houses and meaderies in addition to traditional southwest Pennsylvania wineries.

## **Refucilo Winery**
_Refucilo is an interesting one._
Refucilo Vineyard is located in the Uco Valley of Mendoza, Argentina. And if you’re wondering where Pittsburgh comes into play, you’re not alone. To put it simply, the owners have lived in the region for 20 years and, in 2018, decided to open a store in the North Side to share their wines here!
In being a vineyard in the heart of Mendoza, the winery produces styles including Malbec, a grand reserve Malbec blend, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, and a white wine mostly grown in South America- Torrontes.
During our first visit we sampled three wines (the Malbec, the grand reserve blend, and the Torrontes) and were quite impressed with the flavors. The Malbec was a bit more full-bodied than you’d anticipate for the grape, the grand reserve was a bit more mellow, and the Torrontes, well, you really just need to try that one for yourselves!
_Refucilo Winery is located at 907 Western Avenue in the North Side._
## **Jackworth Ginger Beer in Larimer**
Jackworth Ginger Beer is Pittsburgh’s first ginger beer producer, and this one hit the ground running in 2024 with their launch of an impressive mix of both alcoholic and non-alcoholic products including traditional, spicy, and more.
What Jackworth manages to execute perfectly is showcasing the versatility of ginger in every creation. The alcoholic and NA options are a start, but this one goes further with adjuncts like habanero to bring spice in the aptly named spicy variant, a full cocktail menu using ginger beer as a star ingredient, and even mocktail options for those who do not indulge. 
While this one may not necessarily be a cider or wine, we love that they’re taking a different look at housemade products and offering a wide array of creations that will make just about everyone happy!
_Jackworth Ginger Beer is located at 6615 Hamilton Ave in Larimer._
## **Apis Mead & Winery in Carnegie**
I am a sucker for a large chalice of mead. This sweet alcohol made from fermented honey is one you don’t hear of too often, but at Apis Mead & Winery in Carnegie this is precisely what you’re going to get.
The spectrum of meads at Apis takes on similar format to that of Arsenal Cider House (above). There are the traditional meads, aged meads, and spiced meads as well as an array of flavored meads that push the boundaries of what you’d expect the drink to be.
Although I would’ve preferred to have a powerfully sweet mead like the kind you can find at the local Renaissance Festival, I am also not one to go against trying something new- especially when honey wine is concerned. 
The ones here taste more like flavored wine than the mead you’d expect, but we’re more than okay with that. If they have it, be sure to try “Honey Moon,” a mead that contains similar yeasts and flavors to a Saison beer. Odd, but quite good.
_Apis Mead& Winery is located at 206 Mary Street in Carnegie._
## **Kingview Mead in Mt. Lebanon**
Kingview Mead in Mt. Lebanon is the South Hills resident meadery and serves up a massive selection of meads, ciders, wine, and more- so much so that you may need several visits to even make a dent in their menu.
During our first visit, we opted to stick to the mead style of menu and found many of the offerings here to be light and delicate, with a strong focus on flavor additions from various fruits and spices to name a few. Although we often prefer richer, more viscous mead personally, those who like an array of flavors will likely find many options to try here!
_Kingview Mead is located at 101 Beverly Road in Mt. Lebanon_
## **Enginehouse 25 Winery in Lawrenceville**
Enginehouse 25 is a unique winery in Lawrenceville located in the basement of the Roberto Clemente Museum. 
In fact, the owner of the museum also owns the winery. You can take a tour of the cellar as part of a tour to the museum, and you can also taste and buy the wines at the adjacent wine bar, Arriba.
Similar to Pittsburgh Winery, all the grapes used for making wine at Enginehouse 25 are shipped in from grape-growing regions around the world including South America and California. Their oak barrels are made from Pennsylvania oak that is actually shipped to Australia, turned into barrels by a famous cooper there, and shipped back. 
These beautiful barrels no doubt contribute to some of the depth of flavor that Enginehouse 25 wines exhibit.
The winery focuses mostly on red wines including Cabernet, Merlot, Malbec, and Sangiovese. At the moment they have one white wine, a Riesling. A tasting flight here costs $10, and you can also order gourmet charcuterie and cheese boards to accompany your wine. The cheese selection rotates and is thoughtfully curated by the Wheel and Wedge cheese shop.
Although the price of these wines is fairly steep (with bottles starting at $30), Arriba is definitely a place worth visiting to sample the wines and have a glass or two. If you love Pittsburgh sports you will also love Enginehouse 25 wines, as many of the labels feature photos of local sports figures as well as the legendary Roberto Clemente.
_Enginehouse 25 Winery is located at 3339 Penn Avenue in Lawrenceville._
## **Hog Dog Winery in Reserve Township**
Hog Dog Winery opened up in Reserve Township (just outside of Spring Garden north of the city) in May 2016 and has several dozen white, red, and flavored wines available for sampling and purchase.
We fell in love with the flavored wines that are available, with the cranberry pomegranate, pear, and the 18% alcohol banana being some of our favorites thanks to their robust and lingering flavors. The winery is also known for more unique concoctions, with tomato, pumpkin, and watermelon being some of the more unusual that have been out since they’ve opened.
We left with a few bottles and are looking forward to making some incredible sangria with them at home soon!
_Hog Dog Winery is located at 3500 Spring Garden Avenue in Reserve Township._
## **Courtyard Winery in the Strip District**
Courtyard Winery opened a tasting room in the Strip District in early 2017. Their estate is located in the town of North East, PA, near the New York border on the shores of Lake Erie, and produces all manner of wines from dry to sweet. One of the owners was a former president at Welch’s, so you know that the experience with grapes is vast. 
Many of the wines we sampled from this estate are blends, which help bring out some nuanced flavors in grape varieties you wouldn’t expect- in a good way of course. So next time you are in the Strip District stop by for a sampling of this very tasty vineyard!
_Courtyard Winery’s Strip District location is at 108 19th Street._
## **Greenhouse Co-op in Greenfield**
What do you get when you combine one part cider house and one part plant shop? Greenhouse Co-op in Greenfield, that is what.
This small shop opened in early 2024 to combine to of our favorite things in a single spot- ciders and plants. Grab a glass of their ciders, ranging from traditional to floral infused, and either grab a seat to enjoy the array of plants in the gorgeous setting or, as we prefer, shop!
While Greenhouse Co-op is a bit on the smaller side, the setting here is perfect whether you can snag a seat or are standing to peruse their wonderful offering of plants!
_Greenhouse Co-op is located at 557 Greenfield Ave in Greenfield._
## **Wooden Door Winery in New Kensington**
Wooden Door Winery in New Kensington is about 35 minutes from downtown Pittsburgh to the north east on route 28. Located on the grounds of a gorgeous homestead, this vineyard offers several cozy seating areas and a large selection of wine made from locally grown grapes.
As we know that the grapes in Pennsylvania tend to make for the best sweet wine, we stuck to those during our visit. Many of these are blended into proprietary names rather than just one grape variety at this vineyard (although they have a selection of those, too), so you would do well asking what grapes go into each blend prior to ordering.
Our favorite of the bunch was not a blend, and was the seasonal Autumn Riesling which was a refreshing, sweet Riesling with just a hint of fall spice that was not overpowering like is the case in most spiced wines. 
The vineyard also does cider and even wine slushies using a mix of several wines which, although not traditional in any case, was incredibly refreshing on a hot end-of-summer day.
Wooden Door Winery also advocates responsible drinking rather hard compared to most, and even offers a shuttle service for those who drank too much or would like to go to a nearby business- a nice touch you do not see everywhere that we can always appreciate.
Overall, Wooden Door Winery is a solid estate that should have something for everyone!
_Wooden Door Winery is located at 4087 Greenwood Road in New Kensington, PA. They also have a second location at 101 Custer Avenue in Vandergrift, PA._
## **Greendance Winery in Mount Pleasant**
Greendance Winery at Sandhill is a beautiful property located just outside of Mt Pleasant, about 40 miles southeast of Pittsburgh. The complimentary tastings they offer include 6 wines of your choice, ranging from dry to semi-dry to semi-sweet to sweet and even dessert wines and ports. 
We thought that many of the wines we tried here were pretty dry, even some of the semi-sweet to sweet wines. Our favorite wine that we tried was the Isabella, a sweet blush wine.
One of the best things about this property is that they are also a fruit farm and have a strong focus on growing their own berries and apples. This means you can pick up some incredible products ranging from fresh fruit, pies, preserves, to fruit wines. 
Naturally, if you’re visiting a fruit farm you have to try their pie, and on our recent visit we tried a slice of brambleberry (mixed berries) and blueberry after our wine tasting- a must!
_Greendance Winery is located at 306 Deerfield Road just outside of Mount Pleasant._
## **Greenhouse Winery in Irwin**
Irwin’s resident winery, Greenhouse Winery, first opened in 2007. Since then they have undergone significant expansion including several satellite locations for wine tastings and bottle sales throughout Pennsylvania.
We first visited Greenhouse Winery at a satellite location near Pittsburgh that has since closed, but made the trip down to their idyllic tasting chateau on the top of a hill in the middle of nature in Irwin. The winery is a gorgeous building perfect for events and weddings, and even has a lot of other side amenities like a fire pit, horse shoes, bocce, and more
All of the wines here go down quick, and are also low on sulfites for those who have sensitivities to wine. Our favorites included April Showers, a semi-sweet wine with hints of peach, as well as the Pomegranate (especially in slushie form!). The latter is among the more special creations this vineyard makes as they mix the remaining fruit wine of any given batch with a standard wine. 
If this is your kind of wine, keep one thing in mind- they’re only around for a while and once they’re gone no one knows when they come back!
_Greenhouse Winery is located at 1048 Pinewood Road in Irwin, PA. They also have several other tasting rooms around Pennsylvania outlined on their website._
## **Glades Pike Winery in Somerset**
Glades Pike Winery is one of those places you can’t miss when driving in the Laurel Highlands. This one is located just minutes from the likes of Hidden Valley, Kooser State Park, and Laurel Hill State Park and is a great stop after a long day out in nature.
While this one has a modest tasting room, the wine list more than makes up for that with ample dry wines, sweet wines, fruit wines, and more available to try in a flight. On the dry side this one had an impressive lineup of grapes you may not normally see in Pennsylvania such as Malbec, Tempranillo, and Malbec which are sourced from California and vinified on site.
Truly something for everyone indeed!
_Glade Pikes Winery is located at 2208 Glades Pike, PA-31 in Somerset, PA._
## **Winfield Winery in Cabot**
Winfield Winery is a small winery located in Cabot, PA, a few miles from Todd Nature Reserve. But in the case of this particular winery, when we say small we mean it as they are located in a single family home! 
Although this one lacks in size they make up for it with a sizable wine menu containing a full spectrum of dry, semi-dry, and sweet wines as well as plentiful fruit wines including creations we have not seen at others such as plum and yellow raspberry.
Drop by this one next time you’re in the region for their free tastings and affordable bottles!
_Winfield Winery is located at 1026 Winfield Road in Cabot, PA._
## **Raccoon Creek Winery**
Raccoon Creek Winery is the resident winery at Kramer’s Greenhouse near Hillman State Park and shares the bar space with the greenhouse’s brewery venture, Coal Tipple Brewery.
As with most wineries in the region, the wine making endeavor started as a way to preserve the leftover fruit from the harvests- so you shouldn’t be surprised to find out that the vast majority of the wines here are sweet and are made with ingredients other than grapes.
During our visit we were able to sample wines such as the Riesling (a dry variant that tasted like a crisp, green apple that is highly acidic), raspberry mead, kiwi pear, and even their own hard cider with four rather large pours coming in at just $7. 
While we were not as impressed with the beer from Coal Tipple (mostly due to the brewery’s young age), the wine at Raccoon Creek Winery shines and fruit wine lovers will surely be walking away with a bottle after a tasting (as we did with the kiwi pear).
_Raccoon Creek Winery is located next to Hillman State Park at 1905 Steubenville Pike in Burgettstown, PA._
## **Washington Winery in Washington**
The tasting room for Washington Winery is located right in the heart of Washington, PA, and feels more like a wine accessory store over a winery (thanks in part due to the wealth of brewing equipment they sell on-site). What we like about this winery is that their offering runs the spectrum from those made with grapes imported from California and aged in wine barrels to sweet fruit grapes and more.
So whether you visit this one for a glass or get some bottles to go, odds are good you’ll find several that are to your liking.
_Washington Winery is located at 202 S Main Street in Washington, PA._
## **La Casa Narcisi Winery in Gibsonia**
When we pulled up to La Casa Narcisi Winery in Gibsonia we were immediately impressed: this is one of the few wineries in the Pittsburgh region that has a full-on estate feel complete with perfectly manicured grounds and a beautiful tasting room. It was hard to believe we were just 30 minutes from downtown Pittsburgh!
The winery uses grapes that are all grown in Pennsylvania- many from the Lake Erie region, and a few varietals that are grown right on the estate in Gibsonia.
The tasting room offers three complimentary samples of wines ranging from very dry reds and whites, to semi-sweets, to full on sweet wines, and even fruit wines. While we were predictably not fans of the super dry ones, we found the sweeter wines like the Concord, Niagara, Peach, Riesling, and Moscato to be much more balanced and structured than other sweet wines we’ve tried from the region.
You could spend a whole evening at Casa Narcisi as they have a full restaurant with outdoor seating in a pretty courtyard (the sun-dried tomato dipping oil is heavenly). Several nights a week they also have live music on their outdoor stage. 
_La Casa Narcisi Winery_ is located at 4578 Gibsonia Road in Gibsonia.
## **Vinoski Winery in Belle Vernon**
Vinoski Winery opened in Westmoreland County in 2017, and from the moment you drive up to the estate you’ll feel like you’ve been transported straight to Napa. The reason for this is that (if you haven’t guessed from the photo) the word estate is a bit of a misnomer and the winery is located on the ground floor of a modern day castle.
What makes this one interesting is that the vast majority of the wines here are actually made in California at a property run by the Vinoski family, and the bottles are shipped back to Pennsylvania to be sold locally. So if you are a fan of New World, West Coast wines, this is the place for you (but they do have a few local, sweet wines for lovers of Concord and Niagara).
Five generous samples come in at $10, and samples of the premium collection will set you back $20- a steep price, but also worth it to try wines you just wont get locally as they also do not sell by the glass. Our personal favorite was the Riesling which was quite floral, almost Gewurztraminer like, and we left with two bottles to savor back home.
But with an estate like this, we really wished we could’ve cracked a bottle open while we were there. 
**We will be back for the ambiance alone!**
_Vinoski Winery is located at 333 Castle Drive in Belle Vernon, PA._
## **Christian W Klay Winery near Ohiopyle**
Christian W Klay Winery is one of the closest to Ohiopyle State Park, making it the perfect stop to quench your thirst after a long day of hiking.
The winery sits on a patch of beautiful countryside where you can sit out and enjoy more traditional wines like their Blanc de LaFayette (a floral white) or Nemacolin Castle (a semi-dry similar to Riesling/Gewurztraminer) or some more unique creations like their Spiced Apple or Lavender Mist sweet sparkling wine- a personal favorite.
Most bottles at this winery cost between $14 and $22, making them a bit on the higher side for some local wineries; however, their prices are more than justified as they are as solid as they come for PA wines! Enjoy a bottle while there, take a few to go, and bask in the beauty that is southern Pennsylvania.
For those who want a bit more fortification in their beverages, head across the street to check out Ridge Runner Distillery for their moonshine and affordable cocktails as well. A perfect combo!
Christian W Klay Winery is located at 412 Fayette Springs Road in Chalkhill, PA- just outside of Ohiopyle. Ridge Runner Distillery is located at 417 Fayette Springs Road just across the street.
## **More Southwestern Pennsylvania Wineries Coming Soon**
We’re continually visiting new local wineries and and will be updating this guide as we discover new ones worth your time in the region!

https://www.discovertheburgh.com/places-.data:
Published by Jeremy. Last Updated on December 9, 2025.
_Disclaimer_ : Our site uses demographic data, email opt-ins, display advertising, and affiliate links. Please check out our Terms and Conditions. Pricing, operating hours, or menus may have changed since our initial visit and may not be reflected in subsequent updates. Please confirm these directly with any business prior to visiting. To see more of our content, set us as a Preferred Source in Google.
One of our favorite activities when going out and exploring Pittsburgh is trying new restaurants, and over the years we’ve visited hundreds upon hundreds of local establishments from street food vendors to mom and eateries, fancy prix fixe dining experiences, and everything in between.
Truly, there is no cuisine type we won’t try, and we’ve been on a mission to taste it all.
Since the early days of running _Discover the Burgh_ , we’ve always highlighted a list of our 10 favorite restaurants in our Pittsburgh restaurants guide as a quick call out to the best spots right now. But in that guide, we did not spend a lot of time explaining _why these restaurants made the cut_.
While we thought our linked reviews typically speak for themselves for detailed accounts of a specific dining experience, in this one, we thought we’d take a high-level look at our 10 favorites and share why they’ve made the current list.
But before getting into it, we should note that while these are our personal top 10 places to eat in Pittsburgh, it is hard to compare any two on the list. Is there a big difference between #1 and #2 or #5 and #9 in terms of quality? Not really- they’re all great, and that’s the point. We could spend hours discussing the finer details of why we arranged the list as we did, but in reality, it is just our preference, and any spot on this list is going to offer a great meal.
Likewise, we should call out that these are not Pittsburgh food institutions that have been local staples for decades, nor do these restaurants necessarily sell what we’d call famous Pittsburgh foods. These are _the best restaurants_ without any caveats. So if you’re visiting the city and want to dive more into the local food scene with historic or regional ties, we recommend checking the previously linked articles out, too.
So let’s jump into our 10 favorites now!
### 🏨 **Book a Hotel in Pittsburgh**
  1. **Great Value:** Drury Plaza offers excellent prices downtown.
  2. **Good Views:** Sheraton Station Square features stellar views from river-view rooms.
  3. **Free Parking:** Hampton Inn Strip District includes free parking and a great location.


🏡 Looking for an apartment rental? Find a deal on Airbnb!
## **1. Apteka**
Apteka in Bloomfield has been our favorite restaurant in Pittsburgh for many years, and given its style, vegan Eastern European, you may be a bit surprised. We’re not vegan in the slightest, but oh do we love properly cooked vegetables!
To call what Apteka does with vegetables masterful is an understatement, and this one brings out some stellar flavors that really showcase the versatility of each ingredient. As such, you shouldn’t be surprised to hear that Apteka was nominated for a James Beard Award for Best Chef in the Mid-Atlantic category. Yes, it is really that good.
Be on the lookout for the kluski slaskie (potato dumplings) and pierogi (arguably the best in the city) as these two dishes, amongst others, have us returning time and time again to try their latest takes with seasonal ingredients. Their food program is rounded out with a full bar program full of natural wine, flavorful cocktails, and delightful housemade cordials that really help make each meal sing.
If you are able, be sure to visit a second time in late January / early February for their annual vegan burger pop-up, Crapteka, which features “vegan junk food” of beet, buckwheat, and mushroom burgers plus fries and sunflower seed milkshakes. We recommend getting in line well before they open, as this one is perhaps even more sought after than their regular menu!
_Apteka is located at 4606 Penn Avenue in Bloomfield. They accept extremely limited reservations; otherwise, they offer first-come, first-served seating. Get in early to put your name on the waitlist (we always arrive right when they open, if not just before) and head to a nearby bar like Tina’s, Trace Brewing, or Two Frays Brewing if you want to grab a drink nearby._
## **2. Fet-Fisk**
Fet-Fisk, a Scandinavian-inspired restaurant in Bloomfield (and another James Beard-nominated restaurant), transports us to northern Europe with every bite. Although the restaurant’s name translates to fatty fish, a nod to their seafood origins, this one focuses on a wide array of dishes with Appalachian ingredients for a hybrid menu that is Scandinavia meets Pittsburgh.
Dishes like pickled mackerel with smoked beet and smoked sturgeon pate are straight out of Scandinavia, while others like steak tartare and rye cavatelli feel a bit closer to home. But our absolute favorite dish on the menu here is the roast half chicken with fruit and farmer’s cheese, and yes, we know how crazy that sounds- who recommends a chicken dish anymore?
Fet-Fisk’s chicken is nothing short of masterful. It is marinated in whey from the farmer’s cheese it is served upon, roasted, and topped with seasonal fruit that comes together for a heavenly flavor we have to get on every visit. (The lingonberries in winter are a particular favorite fruit topping!)
For something different, visit on a Monday night for their Crispy Monday feature, which features fried chicken wing flats served on creme fraiche and topped with trout caviar!
Much like Apteka, the restaurant focuses on approachable wines, interesting cocktails, and house-made infusions. Try the marigold schnapps as a digestif if it is on the menu, and be sure to save room for dessert here- their panna cotta (also with seasonal fruit) is divine!
_Fet-Fisk is located at 4786 Liberty Avenue in Bloomfield. They accept reservations for about half of the restaurant and keep a generous number of seats available for walk-ins. But, much like Apteka, we recommend arriving early in case there is a waitlist, especially on weekends._
## **3. Pusadee’s Garden**
Pusadee’s Garden started out as a more conventional neighborhood Thai restaurant in Lawrenceville. But in 2017, they closed for a multi-year remodel and re-opened in 2021 as a high-end Thai fusion restaurant that will have you feeling like you’re eating at a posh resort steps from the beach in Thailand (just, you know, sans beach).
True to its name, the central courtyard at Pusadee’s Garden is an award-winning, beautiful dining garden that is open for outdoor dining on nights with nice weather. Dishes here run the gamut from classic Thai dishes like tom yum soup, green papaya salad, and curry-based dishes to others with a bit more hybrid flair- during one visit, we sampled a stellar yellow curry that was topped with American-style barbecue brisket, which was quite the perfect combination of flavors.
Other popular dishes at Pusadee’s Garden include khao yum- a 17-ingredient salad with tamarind dressing that has been a crowd favorite since the beginning.
_Pusadee’s Garden is located at 5319 Butler Street in Lawrenceville. Advanced reservations are highly recommended; however, on nice nights when the garden is open, additional seating becomes available. For walk-ins on these nights, we recommend arriving before they open to put your name on the waitlist. Head to Allegheny Wine Mixer across the street for the best wine list in the city if they’re open while you wait._
## **4. Morcilla**
It may not be a surprise that we are continuing a global tour of the Pittsburgh dining scene, and Morcilla in Lawrenceville will transport you straight to Spain (where Angie and I spent our honeymoon many years ago).
The menu here is a split of small bites (pintxos), tapas-style plates, and approachable mains with seasonal creations that change frequently. Paired with an impressive cocktail program focusing on Spanish ingredients and flavors, and an equally strong line-up of Spanish wines, there really is a lot to love here!
One dish not to miss is the ox tail montadito- a crispy baguette topped with braised oxtail, caramelized onion, and Mahon cheese. We described this as inverted French onion soup to a server once, and it’s stuck ever since. From there, mix and match the different-sized plates for the meal, consider throwing on a pulpo a la plancha (pictured), and be on the lookout for many of the restaurant’s weekly specials. Some of our favorite dishes here have only appeared on the menu for a limited time!
_Morcilla is located at 3519 Butler Street in Lawrenceville. Advanced reservations are recommended; however, we’ve had good luck with walk-in seating on weeknights- primarily at the bar._
## **5. Fig & Ash**
Fig & Ash in the North Side is the only modern American restaurant in this list, and it earns a spot in our Top 10 for good reason- nearly everything on the menu is cooked over fire on an open hearth.
When this restaurant first opened, the owners completely gutted the first floor of its building down to the frame and rebuilt it from the ground up to support the wood-fired kitchen. This extra effort was worth it as you can really taste the flavor in every bite.
Modern dishes here, like a double-cut pork chop and braised beef short rib, complement sides like roast heirloom carrots with honey whipped ricotta, marcona almond, and sage brown butter, plus so much more. A particularly interesting dish here is their short rib and pork belly meatloaf, which, while unconventional, balances a perfectly beautiful texture with, you guessed it, woodfired flavor. When Angie’s mom first ordered this one, we thought she was a bit crazy, but, much like Fet-Fisk’s chicken, this one has become a favorite of ours that we order regularly.
Fig & Ash is also home to one of the best restaurant cocktail programs in the city, and their inventive drinks have us returning for a round as much as their dinner menu has us coming back for food!
_Fig& Ash is located at 514 E Ohio Street in the North Side. Advanced reservations are recommended; however, they accept limited walk-in seating- primarily at the bar._
## **6. Golden Gai**
Golden Gai by the Richard DeShantz Restaurant Group is actually the second restaurant in their Japanese dining series- a follow-up from their immensely popular Gi-Jin in downtown Pittsburgh.
For many years, Gi-Jin retained this spot in our Top 10 list for being home to some of the freshest, best-tasting raw seafood you can find in the city that was truly in a league of its own. While the quality is still true to this day, its small size, difficulty in getting reservations, and limited menu have us heading to Golden Gai more and more.
This is because, in our opinion at least, Golden Gai offers a very similar sashimi menu to Gi-Jin, but adds on perfectly executed hot dishes like kara-age (Japanese fried chicken), miso black cod, yakitori, and so much more- giving a wealth of options for those looking for more than just raw seafood, while also being a bit easier to score a reservation.
Be sure to grab some of their inventive Asian-inspired cocktails as well, as the bar program is among the best in the city. For a Japanese izakaya, we really can’t ask for much more here. Get some food. Get some drinks. Repeat as long as you can keep eating. Just save room for dessert, too!
_Golden Gai is located at 116 Bakery Square Blvd in Bakery Square. Advanced reservations are highly recommended._
## **7. Dish Osteria**
Pittsburgh is home to many Italian restaurants, and it is really hard to pick a favorite as many offer stunning dining experiences. But when we were traveling in Sicily and not exactly ready to come home, our thoughts immediately shifted to dreaming of our next meal at Dish Osteria in South Side!
_We made a reservation before we even boarded our plane._
Dish Osteria has been serving up classic Italian dishes for over 25 years and hits the mark for perfect execution, incredible hospitality, a killer wine list, and an overall authenticity that would fit in among any restaurant in Sicily.
Yes, you’ll want to snag a reservation at this one several weeks out. But with patience comes a great reward, and within a few bites you’ll quickly understand why Dish is so popular.  _It is just classic Italian food done right!_
Don’t miss this gem that has been a star in Pittsburgh’s dining scene for far longer than any other restaurant on this list!
_Dish Osteria is located at 128 S 17th Street in South Side. Advanced reservations are highly recommended; however, they may have limited walk-in seating- primarily at the bar. Late-night reservations are often regularly available as well._
## **8. The Parlor Dim Sum**
The Parlor Dim Sum is one of several restaurants in Lawrenceville owned by Roger Li. This one began as a dim sum pop-up during the pandemic, which immediately blew up in popularity. Shortly thereafter, Chef Li opened the restaurant in a brick-and-mortar space in his former Ki Ramen location (classics from that spot can still be found on the menu at Nanban nearby).
If you are hungry, be prepared for a feast here. But given that this one focuses on family-style, Cantonese dining, you’ll do well to go with friends and order as much as you can (while adding on some of their impressive cocktails with Asian flavors as well)!
The menu here is quite large, and is split into numerous categories like rice-based, noodles, soup and congee, dim sum, wok-based dishes, and signature Cantonese BBQ, to name a few. You’ll do well to order a bit of everything here to get a full cross-section of the menu, and given their large portions, it is exactly why our recommendation to take friends is warranted.
_You really will want to try a little bit of a lot here!_
Although we always advocate starting with some of their namesake dim sum, our personal favorite dish is the cha siu roasted pork with ginger honey glaze. For first timers, however, we recommend trying this as part of their trio rice plate that comes with a hearty serving of three Cantonese meats- roast duck, chai siu pork, and poached chicken. The entree is big enough for four to share a bite or two of each, and really lets you go down the rabbit hole to find a favorite for your next visit.
Perhaps one of our favorite things about The Parlor Dim Sum is that it always feels like we’re getting a feast for a very reasonable price as well (when splitting with friends, at least), and we always walk out planning our next visit right away.
_The Parlor Dim Sum is located at 4401 Butler Street in Lawrenceville. Advanced reservations are recommended; however, we’ve had good luck with walk-in seating on weeknights._
## **9. Poulet Bleu**
Poulet Bleu is the second restaurant from the Richard DeShantz Restaurant Group in our Top 10, and focuses on classic French dining with a classic, yet high-end, ambiance.
Poulet Bleu was one of our Top 10 favorite restaurants for many years before suffering a long-term closure due to water damage in 2022. After three long years of renovations, the restaurant returned to its former glory in late 2025, bringing back the classic dishes we love in a newly updated space.
Entrees here, like steak frites, Parisienne gnocchi, and roast duck, hit all the notes of traditional French cuisine. Don’t forget to add on appetizers like a perfect bowl of French onion soup and the highly coveted Aligot potatoes served topped with Comte and Gruyère. But to really make the meal complete, be sure to place an order for their famous chocolate souffle when deciding on your entrees. This one takes a while to cook, so you need to commit early, but a perfectly light and fluffy souffle will be your reward to wind down your meal.
There is a reason why Poulet Bleu has been a go-to anniversary spot of ours for many years, and this one delights on every visit.
_Poulet Bleu is located at 3519 Butler Street in Lawrenceville. Advanced reservations are highly recommended._
## **10. DiAnoia’s**
DiAnoia’s is the second Italian restaurant in our Top 10 list, and can be found in the Strip District just outside of the bustling shopping district nearby.
This restaurant is a bright and fun space for all things modern Italian dining, with dining options available for breakfast, lunch, and dinner throughout the week. Classic dishes like cacio e pepe, aglio e olio, and steak florentine find their way on the menu along with fun twists like gnocchi served in a Sorrentina bread bowl (and a pumpkin option in the fall!).
For breakfast, DiAnoia’s has classic dishes ranging from more conventional American breakfasts to delightful frittatas and baked goods from their bakery, Pane e Pronto. Be sure to order some of their zeppole, Italian doughnuts, for breakfast or for a post-dinner dessert! (And if you’re looking for a slice of pizza, be sure to visit Pizzeria Davide next door, too!)
Going beyond the food, DiAnoia’s has a strong bar program, with many Italian specialties (get a Spritz) as well as one of the largest Amari collections in the city.
_DiAnoia’s is located at 2549 Penn Avenue in the Strip District. Advanced reservations are highly recommended._

Published by Jeremy. Last Updated on May 28, 2026.

Pittsburgh can be quite difficult for someone who is not used to the roads. Downtown Pittsburgh is triangular rather than on a square grid, highways are built on top of highways, and there are many road oddities all throughout the city.
That being said, we can say that there are _many_ options to get around Pittsburgh for those looking to visit or live in the city. The following is a selection of the very best recommendations we can provide.
### 🏨 **Book a Hotel in Pittsburgh**
  1. **Great Value:** Drury Plaza offers excellent prices downtown.
  2. **Good Views:** Sheraton Station Square features stellar views from river-view rooms.
  3. **Free Parking:** Hampton Inn Strip District includes free parking and a great location.


🏡 Looking for an apartment rental? Find a deal on Airbnb!
## **Get In From the Airport**
Downtown Pittsburgh is located approximately 20 miles from the airport. Upon exiting the airport take 376 East until you pass through the Fort Pitt tunnel and emerge in downtown.
Typical drive times from the airport are approximately 25-30 minutes without traffic; however, during rush hour or on game days traffic may build up at Green Tree Hill and also at the 376/79 interchange. It is not uncommon for the drive to take an hour or longer at these times.
**For those without a car** , the 28X Airport Flyer departs every 35 minutes from early morning to late at night with stops in Downtown, Uptown, Oakland, Shadyside, and East Liberty. For the full bus schedule, please check out times and stops at the Pittsburgh Regional Transit website.
A more detailed breakdown of how to get into the city from the airport can be found here.
## **Get Around the City By Car**
Driving in Pittsburgh is not the easiest thanks to a few reasons:
  * First, downtown is arranged in the shape of a triangle and not a square grid like most cities.
  * Second, lane expansion is not the easiest task and you may find that multiple roads exist going along similar paths as some are, quite literally, built on top of the previous ones.
  * Finally, our drivers are often too polite and will slam on their breaks to let someone on an on-ramp or perform a Pittsburgh left (letting the first car at a light turn left in front of oncoming traffic).


These oddities often pose problems for visitors who think they are on the right road but then later find they are on the wrong one and have no clear and easy way of getting where they wish to go. As a result, we highly recommend having an updated GPS when traveling through Pittsburgh.
Likewise, keep in mind that many neighborhoods in Pittsburgh have permit parking for residents and have restricted visitor parking to less than 1-2 hours (also be aware of street cleaning schedules). Metered parking is readily available in commercial areas and most meters now accept credit card- although a few coin-operated ones still remain. Likewise, Downtown Pittsburgh, the stadium areas on the North Side, and the Strip District all have pay-per-parking lots available with variable rates that change based on the day of the week, the number of hours parked, or if an event is going on.
## **Get Around the City By Bus**
Pittsburgh public transportation has a fairly robust network that reaches most corners of the city, including the 28X service to the airport. Keep in mind that many routes terminate downtown so you may have to prepare for a minimum of one transfer to get around. This also means that the buses tend to get stuck in the same rush hour traffic as everyone else, so depending on where you’re going you may have to plan to arrive earlier than anticipated.
Pittsburgh city buses also require exact change for payment and have several payment restrictions and other details that users of the public system should be aware of. A full guide to the costs, payment methods, and schedules can be found on the Pittsburgh Regional Transit website.
## **Other Transportation Options**
In addition to public buses, Pittsburgh has a few additional transit options, including the following:
  * **The Inclines** – The last remaining historical funiculars that go up and down Mount Washington. The two inclines are about a 15-minute walk from each other. 
    * The Monongahela Incline connects to the T at Station Square (bottom) and provides easy access to the shops at Shiloh Street on Mount Washington (top).
    * The Duquesne Incline offers the iconic view of Pittsburgh on Mount Washington (top) and has a parking lot at the bottom for visitors. This incline is also next to the fine-dining options on Grandview Avenue.
  * **The T (Light Rail)** – Train that connects the southern suburbs to downtown and the stadiums. 
    * **The T is free for transit within downtown** (First Avenue to Allegheny stops only).
    * Proposed extensions to the T have been made to go to Oakland and the Airport, but don’t hold your breath on this happening any time soon.
  * **POGOH Bikes** – POGOH bike kiosks are available in dozens of spots around the city with a modest fee.
  * **University Shuttles** – Students of the University of Pittsburgh, Chatham, and Carnegie Mellon can ride their respective university shuttle for free when they present their ID card.
  * **Hotel Shuttles** – Many Pittsburgh hotels offer complimentary shuttles within a 1, 2, and 3 mile radius. We recommend reconfirming shuttle options prior to booking if this is a priority as availabilities could change.
  * **Rideshares** – Uber and Lyft services are available in Pittsburgh and cross-town rates start at $15-20 and airport transfers begin at $40-$50 on average but can surge to over $100 late at night. In our experience, Lyft is often slightly cheaper than Uber, but your mileage may vary.


**Have any questions about navigating Pittsburgh?** Comment below! We are always happy to help out.

## **Shadyside History and Map**
Up through the mid-1800s, Shadyside was primarily farmland. Around the time when Shadyside was annexed by the city, a train station opened which is said to have been named Shadyside due to its “shady lanes” (other sources, however, sometimes refer to the farms as being named Shadyside, too).
From there, a mix of industry and residences moved into the neighborhood. As the industry started to pull back away from the East End in the decades that followed, the residential side of the neighborhood grew.
Today, Shadyside is primarily residential with three distinct business districts- one on Walnut Street, one on S. Highland Avenue, and one on Ellsworth Avenue. While distinctly separate, they are all in close proximity for a short drive or a brief walk.
Shadyside is located in the geographic center of Pittsburgh and is fairly easy to define its borders. The neighborhood runs from Centre Avenue to the North (with a small cut-out at Baum on the west side), N. Neville Street to the West, Fifth Avenue to the South, and Penn Avenue to the East.
As Centre Avenue is a vibrant business district that borders East Liberty, many often lump the businesses on the Shadyside half of the street in with that neighborhood outright (we typically do as well). One of the biggest reasons for this is because the East Busway and a set of railroad tracks run just a block or so south of Centre and feels like a more definitive boundary than Centre Avenue.
As such, we often consider Centre to be the de facto northern border of Shadyside- especially when closer to the business district in East Liberty.
## **Attractions in Shadyside**
While we wouldn’t say that Shadyside is particularly known for its attractions, there are a few spots you really must see here. 
The first is Roslyn Place just off of Ellsworth Avenue. This is one of the last remaining wooden streets in the country and is a relatively unique sight that is practically hiding in plain sight.
To visit this one, we  _do not_ recommend driving into Roslyn Place as it is a dead-end road that is often tight for cars (also, it is a residential street so be courteous to those who live there). Instead, we recommend parking on Ellsworth and walking over to check this one out when you are in the neighborhood- it’ll be a whole lot easier!
The second is The Pittsburgh Tattoo Art Museum located on Walnut Street. This unassuming tattoo shop has a lovely collection of artifacts and exhibits focusing on traditional American tattooing in the early 1900s. Great for a quick stop!

Looking for a new restaurant in Shadyside to try? Some of our favorites include the following:
  * Fujiya Ramen – A Japanese restaurant focusing on ramen and rice bowls.
  * Girasole – A critically acclaimed Italian restaurant often considered one of the best in the city.
  * Pamela’s P&G Diner – A popular local breakfast chain known for their delicious hotcakes.
  * The Yard – A gastropub with a strong focus on grilled cheese sandwiches.
  * Mercurio’s – Traditional wood-fired Italian pizza and homemade gelato. A taste of Italy.
  * Cafe Moulin – French cafe serving crepes and other quick eats.
  * Senyai Thai Kitchen – Classic Thai dining in an unassuming house.
  * Lilith – A cozy restaurant tucked away from the business district in Shadyside with unique flavors.
  * Nak Won Garden – A popular Korean restaurant right in the heart of Shadyside.
  * Tocayo – A delightful Mexican restaurant with some stellar tacos and a strong mezcal menu.
  * Soba – An Asian fusion restaurant by the Big Burrito restaurant group.
  * Palm Palm – An international fusion tapas restaurant with coastal vibes.
  * Umi – A high-end sushi and sashimi bar serving up 7 and 11 course omakase meals. Located above Soba.
  * Mad Mex – Tex Mex fare with a twist from this chain from the Big Burrito restaurant group.
  * Casbah – A third restaurant from Big Burrito, all about higher-end Mediterranean fare.
  * Millie’s – An outpost for the popular local ice cream chain.
  * SubZero Ice Cream – An ice cream shop in Shadyside made with liquid nitrogen.
  * Noodlehead – Thai street food restaurant with delicious noodles and amazing prices.


## **Bars in Shadyside**
While the bar scene in Shadyside is small, there are a few you may be interested in:
  * Cappy’s – A modest pub and bar in Shadyside.
  * Urban Tap – A modern bar known for having over 100 beers on draft.
  * P’Vino – An independent wine store that does periodic samples and events.


We also have to give a shoutout to PA Libations as well. While not a bar, this store sells 100% made in PA libations and is the city’s second location after first opening in the Strip District!
## **Coffee in Shadyside**
Shadyside has several coffee shops including chains and locally owned spots. A few local favorites include the following:
  * Mechanic Coffee – A Shadyside location for the independent coffee shop started in Verona, PA.
  * The Boredom Set – An artisan coffee shop inside a boutique clothing shop.
  * Delanie’s Coffee – A popular local coffee shop with locations around the city.


## **Parking in Shadyside**
For the most part, the main business districts of Shadyside offer metered street parking on the main roads and permit parking on side streets with limited duration free for non-permit holders (be sure to check the signs).
The one exception to this would be the Walnut Street business district which has a paid parking garage located on Bellefonte Street just behind The Yard restaurant. As parking here can be somewhat limited, if you are visiting this section of Shadyside especially, it may make the most sense to head to the garage and save yourself a few loops around the neighborhood.
## **Hotels in Shadyside**
The only hotel located within Shadyside proper is the luxury hotel Mansions on Fifth. (Read reviews here)
There are many other hotels right at the neighborhood boundary including the Courtyard by Marriott Shadyside and Hyatt House Pittsburgh (both technically in Bloomfield) plus the SpringHill Suites by Marriott in Bakery Square (Larimer/East Liberty). These would all be within a brief walking distance of the main business districts in Shadyside.

neighborhoods in Pittsburgh for a number of reasons. It is home to a large assortment of international grocery stores and retailers, boutique shops, independent merchants, and several of the best restaurants in Pittsburgh (many of which feature international cuisine as well).
Although we’ve been down to the Strip District hundreds of times over the years, it seems like every time we visit we discover a new business worth exploring and shopping at.
