# Audi Car Show
##### **Weekend July 17-18, 2027**
The Audi Club of Western PA has been a longtime supporter of our event and its members serve on may of our committees. They put on an intimate car show with a great view of the track. All Audi owners are welcome to be in the show and Audi enthusiasts are encourage to stop by.
The Audi tent and display area is located near the Food Truck Courtyard, overlooking German Hill and turns 14 and 15. This is the same location as past years. Enter through Gate E on Schenley Drive. Pre Registered cars can enter starting at 7:00 AM. Non-registered cars must wait until 9:30 am if there is space available. Show ends at 5:00 PM. The event held rain or shine. Sorry – there are no single-day discounts.
##### Contact
Ed Kaczkowski is coordinating the Audi Club display at Schenley Park. Please contact Ed with any questions.
##### Registration to open in 2027
Cost: $70 donation per car
  * Includes weekend parking on the golf course.
  * Gates open at 7:00 AM.
  * Complimentary PVGP Race Program and decal. 
  * Wristband for driver and one passenger, good for the weekend.
  * Lunches are available for $30 per person on Saturday only.


Online registration closes at midnight on July 15. After that, registration is available only at the gate, and the fee increases by $10. Your registration is a charitable donation that supports the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix and our beneficiary charities. Because registration fees directly support our charitable mission and event operations, they are non-refundable. Thank you for your generosity and support.

# MINI Car Show
## July 18/19, 2026
Flickr Gallery from the 2024 MINI Marque – Click the image above to view the entire album
MINI of Pittsburgh hosts this car show on German Hill. They have a shaded private area with a view of Turn 13. MINI owners have always been great supporters of the Grand Prix Car Show and are well represented on the track – they are the perfect cars to race through Schenley Park!
##### MINI was the PVGP’s 2024 Marque of the Year!
This was the third time that MINI was the marque of the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix. This British icon was previously honored in 2004, then in 2014 and in keeping with the 10-year trend, again in 2024.
Minis were everywhere in 2024. They were on track both weekends and were represented at all of our car shows throughout Race Week.
##### Race Weekend & International Car Show in Schenley Park – July 18/19, 2026
Schenley Park is the scene of one of the area’s largest car shows. The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix stages an International Car Show – a combined show of 20 distinct displays featuring nearly 3,000 cars. Show your MINI on the Bob O’Connor Golf Course at Schenley Park all weekend and watch the vintage races through the city streets. Cars of all makes and years are welcome – including new cars! Enjoy a picnic atmosphere, browse the sponsor tents, visit the vendors, and savor the various food options. The main gate at the intersection of Schenley Drive and Forbes Avenue opens each day at 7:00 AM for pre-registered cars. 
**Cost: $70 donation per car**
Your donation includes:
  * Weekend parking on the golf course for Saturday, July 18 and Sunday, July 19. Single-day registrations are not available.
  * Complimentary PVGP Race Program and event decal.
  * Weekend admission wristbands for the driver and all passengers — a $20 value per person.
  * Access to all Schenley Park Race Weekend activities and car show areas.


Online registration closes at midnight on July 16. After that, registration is available only at the gate, and the fee increases by $10. Your registration is a charitable donation that supports the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix and our beneficiary charities. Because registration fees directly support our charitable mission and event operations, they are non-refundable. Thank you for your generosity and support.
##### Many thanks the team at MINI Pittsburgh for their support!

# Volkswagen Show
##### **Weekend July 18/19, 2026**
The Fresh Air VW Car Club hosts our Volkswagen Show held annually on German Hill in Schenley Park. It overlooks the thrilling Turn 13 on the track, Volkswagen enthusiasts of all makes and models are welcome to join us for one of the premier car events in the City of Pittsburgh.
The Volkswagen area will display all sizes and sorts of Volkswagens for all to remember and reminisce about their memories of these iconic German vehicles. Visit the Fresh Air VW Car Club’s website or Facebook page to keep up with all their activities.
##### Contact
Please contact Cory Anderson of the Fresh Air VW Car Club if you have any questions.
##### Location
The Volkswagen Show is located on German Hill in their traditional spot- enter through **Gate** **E** along Schenley Drive
##### Registration
Schenley Park is the scene of one of the area’s largest car shows on the July 18/19 weekend. The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix stages an International Car Show – a combined show of 20 distinct displays featuring nearly 3,000 cars. Show your vehicle on the Bob O’Connor Golf Course at Schenley Park all weekend and watch the vintage races through the city streets. Cars of all makes and years are welcome, including new cars! Enjoy a picnic atmosphere, browse the sponsor tents, visit vendors and enjoy the various food vendors. The main gate at the intersection of Schenley Drive and Forbes Avenue opens daily at 8:00 AM for pre-registered cars. 
**Cost: $70 donation per car**
  * Gates open at 7:00 AM.
  * Includes weekend parking on the golf course.
  * Complimentary PVGP Race Program and decal. 
  * Wristband for the driver and one passenger, good for the weekend.
  * Online registration closes at midnight on July 16, and you must pay at the gate after that.

# Walnut Street Invitational Car Show
Monday, July 13, 2026
**Experience Automotive Elegance on Walnut Street**
Stroll down Shadyside’s picturesque Walnut Street and take in the sight of 135 rare, classic, and exotic cars lining the block. This one-of-a-kind event offers a preview of the incredible vehicles featured at the upcoming PVGP International Car Show. Celebrated as one of the region’s most anticipated automotive showcases, this exclusive, invitation-only display brings together some of the finest and most unique cars. Don’t miss this unforgettable celebration of automotive artistry.
### Sponsors
The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix welcomes back Piatt Sotheby’s International Realty as the sponsor of the Walnut Street Car Show. Stop by their new offices at 5513 Walnut Street. It’s a popular gathering spot during the car show – stop by and say hello.
* * *
### Invitation Policy
Only cars holding a mailed invitation will be admitted to limit the confusion on the day of the show. The logistics of squeezing 135 cars onto Walnut Street are daunting; accommodating unexpected guests is nearly impossible. Please do not show up without an invitation, expecting to show your car. Invitations are rotated from year to year, allowing us to showcase a different variety each year. Participants are invited to join us for a private party upstairs at Mario’s East Side Saloon during and after the show. Contact **Greg Farrell** for details.
**Online donations are greatly appreciated. Click below to donate to our charities in honor of this show – please understand that a donation does not guarantee that your car will be in the show.**
* * *
###  **Mario’s East Side Saloon hosts our Walnut Street Party, thank you for your support!******
_Mario’s was created by a local Pittsburgh legend named Bob Pessolano in 1982. After 25 years of devotion to his South Side patrons, he retired in 2007 and left his establishment to 3 young professional drinkers who had the foresight to not fix which was not broken… In 2011, Mario’s undertook its first expansion with its sights on Shadyside. After consultation with 2 close friends, Mario’s East Side was born. Today they are a unique blend of Neighborhood, College, and Sport’s Bar all rolled into one. They offer our customers a welcoming and relaxed environment where friends both old and new can hang out, where you can test your wits at Team Trivia, enjoy Karaoke, and catch your favorite sport’s team. It is also the best place to be for a cold one after the PVGP Walnut Street Car Show._
* * *
**Think Shadyside** The Shadyside Chamber of Commerce’s guide to news, events & promotions on Walnut, Ellsworth, Highland and everything in between. Sometimes you just know you’ve got it good. You’re in Shadyside. Boutiques, shops and galleries mingle with national retailers in a neighborhood of tree-lined streets, historic homes, hip events, and distinctive restaurants. And most everything is within walking distance. Convenient to Pittsburgh, yet miles away from the mall. If you’re searching for an extraordinary way to spend a day, a night, or a lifetime, just Think Shadyside!

# American Car Show
##### **Weekend July 17-18, 2027**
The PVGP’s American Car Show has everything from Model A’s to Z-28’s. Featuring all American cars from the early 1900’s all the way up to the present day. Classics, customs, street rods and muscle cars are welcome to the display on the Bob O’Connor Golf Course. This show continues to grow yearly and contains the widest variety of cars on the golf course. Vehicles from every American manufacturer are represented. Car clubs are encouraged to participate as a group and will be parked together, but individual entries are always welcome.
The American Car Show features Ford, Mopar, Buick and Cadillac on the clubhouse side of Schenley Drive with Corvettes and Chevrolets on the track side of Schenley Drive. Electric Avenue, show sponsored by King Electric, is plugged in just below the clubhouse featuring Teslas and all EVs.
This year, Pontiac and Oakland are the Spotlight Cars.
##### Registration to Open in 2027
Schenley Park is the scene of one of the area’s largest car shows on the July 18/19 weekend. The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix stages an International Car Show – a combined show of 20 distinct displays featuring nearly 3,000 cars. Show your vehicle on the Bob O’Connor Golf Course at Schenley Park all weekend and watch the vintage races through the city streets. Cars of all makes and years are welcome, including new cars! Enjoy a picnic atmosphere, browse the sponsor tents, visit vendors and enjoy the various food vendors. The main gate at the intersection of Schenley Drive and Forbes Avenue opens daily at 7:00 AM for pre-registered cars. 
**Cost: $70 donation per car**
Your donation includes:
  * Weekend parking on the golf course for Saturday, July 17 and Sunday, July 18. Single-day registrations are not available.
  * Complimentary PVGP Race Program and event decal.
  * Weekend admission wristbands for the driver and all passengers — a $20 value per person.
  * Access to all Schenley Park Race Weekend activities and car show areas.


Online registration closes at midnight on July 15. After that, registration and payment must be made at the gate and increases by $10. Thank You for Supporting the PVGP’s Charitable Mission Thank you for supporting the PVGP and our charities. This fundraiser supports residential care and treatment for people with autism and intellectual/developmental disabilities. Thanks to your support, we have donated more than $7 million to charity since 1983. Your registration is a charitable donation to the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix and our beneficiary charities. Because these funds directly support our charitable mission and event operations, we are unable to offer refunds. We sincerely appreciate your generosity and support.
Online registration closes at midnight on July 15. After that, registration is available only at the gate, and the fee increases by $10. Your registration is a charitable donation that supports the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix and our beneficiary charities. Because registration fees directly support our charitable mission and event operations, they are non-refundable. Thank you for your generosity and support.
**The American Car Show is a general show for all American Cars. Several other dedicated PVGP car shows offer different pricing and amenities. Visit the links below to learn more and register:**
##### Featured Shows
  * **Enthusiast Grid **A new addition for 2026 that welcomes a new generation of automotive culture and enthusiasts.
  * **Bronco Wild Fund Display** A show for Ford Broncos.


##### General Car Shows
  * **Asian Car Show** Subaru, Mazda, Nissan/Datsun, Honda, Acura, KIA, Mitsubishi, Suzuki, etc.
  * **Overland Adventure Display **A new group that will also act as overnight security.


##### British Car Shows
  * **British Car Day **Saturday, July 17 – Hosted by the WPTA for all British Cars.
  * **MINI Car Show **Hosted by MINI of Pittsburgh.


##### German Car Shows
  * **BMW Pavilion **Hosted by Allegheny Region BMW Club.
  * **Porsche Car Show**Hosted by Allegheny Region Porsche Club of America.
  * **Mercedes-Benz Car Show **Hosted by the Mercedes-Benz Club.
  * **Volkswagen Show** Hosted by Fresh Air VW Club.
  * **Audi Car Show **Hosted by Audi Club.
  * **European Classic& Sports Car Show ** Car show for Saab, Volvo, and other European vehicles not in the listed shows. Open to cars not registered with Audi, BMW, Mercedes, or Porsche clubs. Vehicles park in a separate area and are not eligible for club lunches, refreshments, or activities.


##### Individual Car Shows
  * **Italian Cortile **A Celebration of Italian Cars
  * **French Quarter **All French cars in the Cortile
  * **Cars ‘N’ Coffee **Exotic car display hosted by Cars N Coffee Pittsburgh – invitation only
  * **North Hills Sports Car Club **Club Display
  * **Vintage Motorbike Show **Hosted by Pittsburgh Ton-Up Club for all motorbikes of all makes and years.
  * **Patron Parking** Trackside parking on Sunday, July 18, is open to all cars starting at $200 per spot


##### Location
The American Car Show is held at the Bob O’Connor Golf Course. Cars are displayed on the fairway just below the clubhouse. As you enter Schenley Park from the top of Schenley Drive, you will be directed to enter GATE B on your right.

Email Mark Morrow or Marc Koszak American Car Display Co-Captains with any questions.

# Tune-Up @ SouthSide Works
Wednesday, July 14, 2027
The PVGP looks forward to celebrating our 45th year in 2027 by partying SouthSide Style for our annual Tune-Up as we prepare for the races and car show just a few days later.
Hundreds of cars will gather for a fabulous car show, featuring race cars, exotics, antiques, and show cars, at this exciting street festival in the streets surrounding the SouthSide Works Town Square.
We are looking forward to another great evening on the South Side!
## Registration Opens in 2027
**_Registration closes on Monday, July 12, at noon. Entries will not be accepted after that, and you cannot pay at the event._**
Participation in this year’s Tune-Up Party is still just $50. You get a reserved parking spot within the Automotive Showcase on the streets of the SouthSide Works. Two drink coupons for the driver, redeemable at any drink station, are included. You can also register any guests for $25 each, and they will also receive two complimentary drink coupons. There are plenty of great places to Eat & Drink in Town Square. The PVGP will also have drink trucks available.
**Registration can only be completed through the Vivenu online portal below; there is no day-of registration**. After registering and paying online, please bring a printed receipt or display it on your mobile device to gain entry. Your receipt will include a QR code that can be scanned upon entry to facilitate a quick, touchless process. We strongly encourage you to pre-register now – the event typically sells out, and no day-of entries are available.
* * *
Live Music by the The Brick’s – an acoustic trio vocal band that plays songs by America, The Eagles, CSNY, The Band, Van Morrison just to name a few.
* * *
## Directions and Entry Information
  * To simplify the entry process, please be prepared to display the QR code on your receipt. This code is valid for your entry only and is non-transferable.
  * Registrants should enter the event at S. Water Street and Tunnel Boulevard, near the Hot Metal Bridge, and proceed to 28th Street; **_exceptions are noted below._** Other streets will be blocked off at various locations, and the barriers will remain in place. Once you arrive at the designated entry, volunteers will gladly direct you to a parking spot. Exception groups. Cars and Coffee Members should use the 26th Street and Tunnel Boulevard entrance ONLY. **_These guidelines are in place to ensure quick, efficient parking. Please abide by them accordingly._**
  * Cars may begin arriving at 5:00 PM & should be in place by 6:00 PM. Early arrivals will NOT be accommodated as we have a small window to block the streets and allow entry. We cannot have cars blocking the city streets before 5 pm.
  * Once your car is in place, please proceed toward the Hofbrauhaus to pick up your registration packet. The desk will be at 27th Street and Tunnel Street. Your packet will include your placard (if pre-registered), the drink tickets for the number of people you indicated would be in your car at registration (2 per paid guest), and a decal. The drink tickets are valid for “special PVGP drinks” at the drink trucks located throughout the area.
  * To minimize on-site transactions, there is no need to purchase additional drink tickets for the event. You can purchase additional beverages from the drink trucks listed above.


* * *
****The SouthSide Works is Pittsburgh’s premier city lifestyle center. Uniquely positioned on the Monongahela riverfront and nestled in Pittsburgh’s historic and bustling Southside neighborhood on the former J &L Steel Works site. Visit national retailers and convenience stores, grab a bite to eat, or go out for the night. SouthSide Works is also home to some of the country’s most notable companies and nonprofits, and now, the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Tune-Up!

# Waterfront Car Cruise
Tuesday, July 14, 2026
**4:00 pm – 9:00 pm**
****Join us for a spectacular car show open to all—whether you’re showing off a classic, a modern marvel, a truck, or a motorbike! This is the perfect gathering for auto enthusiasts, hot rodders, gearheads, and car lovers of all kinds. Families are also welcome to come enjoy an evening of stunning vehicles, great company, and unforgettable stories. There will be vendors and food available. Enter from E. Waterfront Drive at Chipotle Mexican Grill.
**Entry: $10 Donation at the Gate**  
No pre-registration is required. Simply make your $10 donation upon arrival. All proceeds benefit our autism charity partners as part of the PVGP, one of the region’s largest charitable events.  
Each participating vehicle will receive a PVGP sticker at entry.
**Thank you to our Sponsors and Partners  
**
If you have any questions about our car cruise, please contact the Grand Prix’s Cruise event captain, Don Privett.
* * *
**Cruise Rules**  
We strive to provide a safe and friendly evening for all and we ask our visitors to abide by some simple rules:
  * There is NO saving spaces – the event fills up almost every year so saving a spot for a friend is not permitted. If you want to park together, we suggest you arrive together.
  * PVGP volunteers will direct you to your parking space
  * Pop-up canopies are not permitted in the cruise area
  * Alcoholic beverages or the consumption of such is strictly prohibited on the premises.
  * For Sale signs and solicitation of vehicles is not permitted.
  * NO solicitation of ANY kind except by approved vendors. Click here for information on becoming a vendor.
  * NO burnouts! We appreciate horsepower as much as anyone, but a crowded shopping center parking lot is not the safest place to do this. If you really want to lay down some rubber why not get a competition license and become a vintage racer!
  * Pets are permitted if on a leash and under the control of the owner. If in the opinion of the PVGP, a pet presents a danger or nuisance to others, the pet owner and pet will be asked to leave.

# Porsche Club Car Show
##### **Weekend July 17-18, 2027**
Plan to attend the 44th annual Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix with the Allegheny Region Porsche Club of America. Join hundreds of your fellow club members, guests from other regions, and friends as they gather on “**Porsche Field** ” in Schenley Park to enjoy fine automotive culture, vintage races, and the camaraderie that defines PVGP weekend.
This year promises to be an outstanding event featuring a multitude of Porsche Club and PVGP events spanning nine days. **Porsche Field** patrons enjoy high-quality amenities, including a catered lunch from Mission BBQ, Dining and Registration tents replete with linen tablecloths, cooling fans, and unlimited non-alcoholic beverages, live music, high-value raffle prizes, and People’s Choice Awards. The club’s PVGP Committee uses a streamlined check-in process in which attendees register through Motorsport Registration (MSR) and receive an email from  __**PVGP_Reg@arpca.com**__ with a dash plaque and a QR code “ticket” as attachments. As members drive up to the Porsche Field, volunteers scan the QR code and have wrist bands, raffle tickets, and the PVGP program pre-staged at the Registration tent.
## Porsche Club Leads PVGP 2020 Fundraising Efforts
In 2020, the Allegheny Region of the Porsche Club of America took a leading role in the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix’s efforts to raise funds for our charities”. Because of the COVID-19 Pandemic, the annual 10-day PVGP was canceled. Instead, the PVGP announced the organization would engage in a “Shifting Gears” campaign for the remainder of the year to raise money for its charities. Local car clubs and supporters staged 26 events that allowed them to safely be together and enjoy meeting with their cars.”
Ed Rice and the Porsche Club raised $6,100 with Parade Laps in Schenley Park on Sunday, July 26, the normally scheduled Race Day. “The impromptu event was a stunning success,” according to Ed Rice, president of the Allegheny Region Porsche Club. “I was in a melancholy mood when the event was canceled and I just didn’t want to sit around and do nothing that weekend. Then I thought, what the heck, every year in the days before Race Weekend in Schenley Park I drive the racecourse to get into the vibe of the PVGP.”
Read the full details in the September issue of Rundschau – the club’s newsletter.
Attend one of the most spectacular vintage races in the world – and Party ARPCA style! The PVGP is the Club’s biggest annual event. Join hundreds of club members, guests from other regions, and friends as they gather on the lawn at Schenley Park to enjoy their cars, races, and above all, the camaraderie that has grown over the years. On March 25, 1961, 31 Porsche owners and P.C.A. members gathered at McSorley’s Restaurant in the North Hills of Pittsburgh to form their own P. C. A. Chapter. Visit the Allegheny Region’s website to learn more about their history. Porsche was the Marque of the Year in 1994 and 2002, each time they set a record for charitable funds raised by the marque including 2011 when $73,500 was raised from the Marque and $200,000 was split between our charities.

# "Evening of Speed" Drivers Reception
Friday, July 17, 2026
Kick off Race Weekend the right way, right at trackside.
The Drivers Reception returned to the Schenley Park Visitor’s Center for the first time since 2021, and there’s no better place to start your weekend. Located beside the Panther Hollow Bridge and directly along the course, this is your chance to step out of the paddock and into the spotlight, surrounded by fellow racers, crews, and fans who appreciate what you bring to the streets of Schenley Park.
From 6:30 PM to 8:00 PM, the track in front of the Visitor’s Center becomes a gathering point for the entire racing community. Cars on display, stories shared, and a relaxed atmosphere that lets you connect with other drivers before the competition begins.
At 6:30 PM, racers will parade from the paddock around the circuit to the reception. They will park their race cars trackside in front of the Visitor’s Center for all to see, with the option to arrive in a support vehicle instead.
Thanks to Broad Arrow Auctions, A Hagerty Company, this is a complimentary event for participants. No tickets, no barriers, just a great evening with the people who make this event special.
****
* * *
### Tickets
Designed as a special gathering for PVGP racers and their teams, this event offers a very limited number of guest tickets. Join us for an exclusive behind-the-scenes experience where you’ll have the opportunity to meet the drivers, view the cars up close, and be part of the racing community.
* * *
### Schenley Park Visitor Center
The Schenley Park Visitor Center sits right where the action happens, alongside the Panther Hollow Bridge and directly on the course, making it a natural home for our Driver Reception. Its recent transformation by the Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy reflects a shared commitment with the City of Pittsburgh to preserve and elevate this historic park while keeping it active and accessible. That same partnership allows the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix to bring racing to these streets each summer, using the restored Visitor Center as a gathering place where drivers, crews, and fans connect in the heart of Schenley Park.

https://pvgp.org/about-us/.page title: About The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix | Vintage Street Race & Charity
https://pvgp.org/about-us/.data:
**_The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix is the nation’s only vintage street race and the largest vintage race event. It includes car shows, parties, parades and motorsport events with the culmination each July in Schenley Park._**
Our original mission, established in 1983, was “To stage a world-class vintage automotive event to raise funds to provide care, treatment and support for individuals with autism and intellectual/developmental disabilities in western Pennsylvania.” 44 years later, we are still on track.
Though our first race was in 1983, our organization actually started the year prior. Art McGovern and Mary Beth Gmitter envisioned the city streets winding through Schenley Park as a perfect venue for vintage auto racing. Told that the City of Pittsburgh’s approval hinged on the assurance that any money raised would go to charity, they first approached Myron Cope of WTAE-TV Sports fame – also an autism awareness advocate. Meetings with the city’s parks people followed, and then-Mayor Richard Caliguiri gave his enthusiastic approval. The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Association, consisting of volunteers, was created, and net proceeds would be donated to charity. In April 1983, during a meeting in vintage racer Alan Patterson’s Shadyside garage, the planning began for the first Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, scheduled for Labor Day 1983.
An incredible amount of work ensued thanks to the volunteers from the Sports Car Club of America and the Vintage Sports Car Club of America. Some 75 entrants raced on what would become known as one of the most challenging vintage courses in the country. Five races, along with a parade of patrons, were scheduled, and the plan was put in motion.
We would be lying if we said that the first year went off without a hitch. The complications of a temporary track in the middle of one of Pittsburgh’s most popular public parks reared their heads almost immediately. Huge fence gaps and the labyrinth of infield trails left the course open to penetration from above and below. Recreational joggers were running with the cars zooming around the track. Our volunteer security struggled to overcome these logistical challenges. Nonetheless, the event was a success.
The experience only fueled our imaginations and motivations, and in 1984 the expansion began. We added an invitational car show and the Sunday tailgate known as Patron Parking. By 1985, our spectator count grew to 40,000 and included participants and fans from all over North America as well as Europe. The genesis of Race Week, in 1987, was ushered in with our first Kick-Off Rallye the preceding Sunday. Our volunteer army grew by leaps and bounds and by 1989 we reached 1,000 volunteers – many of whom still volunteer to this day. Race Week spectator draw has consistently grown throughout the years and is now estimated at close to a quarter-million.
With the added size came added attention – from Pittsburgh and beyond. In 1996, Buick signed on as our first Presenting Sponsor. They also brought new models and concept cars to the event and helped legitimize our stature within the auto industry. Modern race cars from the Indy 500, Le Mans, and elsewhere have blasted down the Boulevard of the Allies and snaked between Serpentine’s stone walls. Ferrari, Marque of the Year in 1993, showed up with museum-piece cars and actually put them on the track – in the rain. In 1994, Marque of the Year one-upmanship began as each attempted to better the proceeding’s donations and spectacle. The gauntlet, first thrown down by Porsche, has been eagerly picked up by BMW, Mustang, MINI and others since then. In 2018 BMW set the Marque record with $126,500 raised only to be surpassed the next year by Ford Mustang & Shelby with $132,500!
Shop ‘n Save took over the Presenting Sponsorship from 2001 through 2013, which oversaw many events being added to occupy 10 straight days of motorsport events. Sponsorship began to grow significantly after that and has led to a larger show, resulting in increased charity donations.
In 2004, the second weekend of racing was added at Pittsburgh International Race Complex, and it has developed into a self-supportive historic racing event for newer historic bug-bore cars that are too fast for the city streets of Schenley Park. Pitt Race closed down after the 2025 season, marking the end of 22 great years of racing.
A black-tie gala was launched in 1997 and has since become a staple of the Pittsburgh summer social scene, ranking among our largest fundraisers. Our Tune-Up party was created in 2006 and has grown into a tremendous event that has since moved to the SouthSide Works.
The Greater Pittsburgh Automobile Dealers Foundation took the wheel as our presenting sponsor in 2014 and the partnership has driven our greatest growth and success through 2022. A Countryside Tour was started and filled Thursday, the last remaining Race Week open day. In 2017 a Jet Center Party was added, elevating our event to the top tier of worldwide automotive events. In 2018 we hosted the BMW Oktoberfest and in 2019 the national car clubs for Shelby and Alfa Romeo held their conventions at the PVGP. We are pleased that they chose to celebrate with us.
The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix has continued to grow while adapting to major challenges and welcoming significant automotive milestones. A highlight was the Shelby Convention’s visit in 2018, which included the unveiling of the 760-horsepower 2020 Ford GT500 during the downtown car show and displays throughout Race Week.
In 2020, the pandemic forced the cancellation of Race Week events, but the PVGP responded with the “Shifting Gears” initiative, encouraging car clubs to hold smaller driving events. More than two dozen gatherings raised $60,000 for charity.
In 2021, Vintage Indy returned with historic Indy 500 cars and two-time winner Al Unser Jr. as Honorary Race Director. Subsequent years featured notable guests and specialty races, including Porsche executive Ray Shaffer as Grand Marshal, a Viper spotlight with Team Viper, and the Kastner Cup Triumph race. In 2023, Shelby Daytona designer Peter Brock and Grand Marshal Luigi Chinetti Jr. praised the event’s authentic vintage racing atmosphere.
Recent highlights include the GT40 Reunion, Ragtime Racers exhibitions, and the debut of the Grand Prix Garden Party at Phipps Conservatory. In 2025 we hosted the Panoz Reunion at Pittsburgh International Race Complex – on of the last events at the track before it was closed.
When the Panther Hollow Bridge closed in 2025, the PVGP created new race layouts, demonstrating the organization’s creativity and resilience while continuing to earn international recognition.
Accolades continue to grow. Classic Motorsports Magazine honored the PVGP as a winner in its inaugural Editors’ Choice Awards. This distinction adds to the event’s expanding international recognition, including its third consecutive nomination as a finalist for “Motorsport Event of the Year” by the International Historic Motoring Awards.
All the while, we’ve held true to our charity mission –to produce a world-class vintage automotive event to raise funds to help provide residential care, treatment and support for autistic and intellectually/developmentally disabled individuals in the Pittsburgh region. It has been over 40 years since a cadre of car nuts met in Alan Patterson’s Shadyside garage, and each year brings its challenges.
Our volunteers remain the heart of the organization and the event, with over 1,000 dedicated individuals working year-round to stage this incredible event. Much credit also goes to our sponsors, racers and participants who share their cars to make our event possible.
Start Your Engines!
_**Dan DelBianco**_  
Executive Director  
Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Association

# General Info & FAQ – Schenley Park
### PVGP Contacts
Competition Director **Joe Teplitz**  
Paddock **Ken Murin** and **Brian Urban**  
Registrar **Mark Hanson**
###  Paddock
The PVGP does not take control of the Schenley Park and Prospect Drive until 8:00 AM on Friday, July 17. If you arrive in town with your trailer and wish to park in the paddock on Thursday, you must do so at your own risk; no PVGP security is provided until Friday night. Ken Murin runs the Schenley Park paddock and will begin assigning your paddock spots promptly at 8:00 AM on Friday. If you are already in the paddock before 8:00 AM Friday, please do not begin unloading, as you may be asked to move to another location or adjust your setup to make more room for others.
Drivers should email Ken Murin with any questions about paddock arrangements. We can fit nearly 150 cars, but it takes careful planning, and it helps if we know any special needs beforehand.
+ The paddock is located in a city park and is open to the general public until 8:00 AM Friday, July.
+ The entrance to the paddock is located at the corner of Hobart Street and Prospect Drive. The paddock itself is located on a city street (Prospect Drive) and surrounding grassy areas.
As a city park, there are no power, water, or sanitation hookups or dump sites provided.
+ No open fires are allowed in the paddock at any time.
+ No PVGP Volunteers will be available to assist you in parking in the paddock until 8:00 AM on Friday.
+ Anyone parking in the paddock before that time must understand that they may be required to move on Friday morning at the discretion of the Paddock Chief.
+ Parking in the paddock is both limited and tight. The shorter your rig’s overall length, the more room you and your fellow competitors will have to park.
+ Rigs in excess of 40 feet overall may be held outside the paddock until approximately 6:00 PM Friday to assess the availability of parking by the Paddock Chief. Parking may be on alternate streets.
+ Race cars only are permitted to park on the asphalt. No bumpers, tent posts, etc, are allowed beyond the painted white lines. We must maintain proper space for emergency vehicles to enter/exit the paddock.
+ Trailers and support vehicles must be parked in the grassy areas throughout the paddock.
+ Each race car entered in the event is allowed one(1) support vehicle to be driven in and out of the paddock on Saturday and Sunday of the event. (NO EXCEPTIONS) All other vehicles must be removed from the paddock area on Friday night.
+ Each driver registering at the event will be given one(1) “Paddock Access Pass” to be permanently attached to the outside of the driver’s side top corner of the windshield of the chosen support vehicle. (NO EXCEPTIONS) Proper placement of this pass will expedite your entry to the paddock.
+ Beginning at 7:00 AM Saturday, July 18, no vehicle will be admitted to the paddock without the pass correctly mounted in the correct position. (NO EXCEPTIONS)
+ Parking for additional vehicles outside the paddock is extremely limited and the owner is responsible for obtaining appropriate parking.
### Refund Policy
Your race entry will be fully refunded if you notify Event Chairman or Registrar before your tires hit the track on Saturday morning.
### Technical Inspection
Scott Buriak runs tech in the paddock  
Friday 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM  
Saturday 8:00 AM-Noon  
**PVGP Tech Inspection Sheet – PDF**
### Special Features
We are hosting the Axis vs Allies Race on Saturday afternoon.
### Track Orientation – July 17
3:00 – 4:30 pm Walking tour of track – mandatory for first-time drivers  
5:00 – 5:35 pm Mandatory Drivers Meeting  
6:00 – 6:30 pm Stage for the parade on the track to the Driver Reception  
6:30 pm Driver Reception at Schenley Park Visitors Center  
8:15 pm Escort cars back to the Paddock
### Fuel
There is no longer a fuel vendor available at Schenley Park – please bring enough race fuel to get you through the event.
### Special Car Requirements
Sound Restrictions: Yes  
Quiet Hours: 8:00 pm to 8:00 am all weekend.  
Antifreeze permitted: No  
Transponder Required: Yes. Cars  _without_ transponders will be gridded by Timing & Scoring and may start in the back. No transponder rentals are available – sorry _.  
_ Refer to our Rules & Regulations for a comprehensive list of vehicle requirements.
### Crew
Two crew members are included, along with the driver, with each race entry. The crew must check in during Registration hours and receive wristbands for access to the HOT PITS.
### Meals
A PVGP authorized food vendor will be set up in the paddock selling breakfast & lunch all weekend. Hours are as follows:  
Friday from 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM  
Saturday from 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM  
Sunday from 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM
### Friday Driver Reception
**Schedule:**
  * **6:30 PM:** Cars depart the grid, travel to Schenley Park Visitor Center across the street from Phipps Conservatory.
  * **6:30–8:00 PM:** Food and drinks served within the Schenley Park Visitor Center
  * **8:15 PM:** Racers return to the paddock via the track – counter track.


### Saturday Dinner
The PVGP hosts a dinner with cold beer from Helltown Brewing 30 minutes after the last race is completed. We welcome racers and their crews to join us for a $25 donation per person that must be made on your MSR entry – no day of admittance.
### Security
As in the past, volunteers will provide some security, but it will be limited. Schenley Park is a public area that cannot be fully closed to the public. All entrants should take precautions for their own security. Close and lock up if no one will be at your trailer.
### Drones
No person in a Pittsburgh City Park shall operate a motorized model airplane, drone or any other mechanized or motorized devices… unless such is conducted in compliance with City Code Chapter 492 (‘Film Permits’) and all applicable federal, state and local law.
### Recreational Vehicles
Drivers/crew only on a very limited basis in the paddock. There are no electrical power or shower facilities available. Overnight stay is not permitted in the CitiPark.
### Hotels
The Hilton Garden Inn University Place is the perfect home base for racers during the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Race Weekend. Located at 3454 Forbes Avenue in the heart of Oakland, the hotel is just minutes from Schenley Park and offers quick, convenient access to the paddock, track, and all Race Weekend activities. The hotel also understands the needs of racers and crews, with special parking accommodations available for race rigs and trailers. A dedicated PVGP room block is available at a special rate of just $179 per night, making it an easy and affordable choice for competitors looking to stay close to the action all weekend long.  
Hilton Garden Inn – University Place  
3454 Forbes Avenue, Pittsburgh, PA 15213  
**Hotel Booking Link**
### What to See and Do in Pittsburgh
There is plenty to do in and around Pittsburgh while you are here for the races. Carnegie Museum and Phipps Conservatory are walking distance from Schenley Park, Squirrel Hill is a mere 5 blocks and downtown is only 5 miles away. See Visit Pittsburgh for details.
### Contacts
Joe Teplitz – Schenley Park Competition Director ‭(646) 258-4000  
Ken Murin – Chief of Paddock ‭(412) 860-7263‬
### Entry Form & Donations
Entries will be accepted through MotorsportReg – **Register Here**. We offer early discounts.

#  ******Pontiac & Oakland – 100th Anniversary  
Spotlight Car Show  
2026 Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix**
A century ago, Pontiac changed the game. In 2026, it takes over Schenley Park.
For Pontiac owners and enthusiasts who have never experienced the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, this is your moment. While PVGP is known worldwide for its vintage racing, at its heart, it is a celebration of all car culture—and this year, American performance takes center stage. The Pontiac & Oakland 100th Anniversary Spotlight invites you to be part of something bigger than a traditional car show: a full-scale festival where your car is not just displayed, it is part of the story.
Bring your GTO, LeMans, Bonneville, Firebird, Trans Am, Grand Prix, Fiero, Safari wagons, or your Oakland-era classic and park it on the fairways alongside thousands of fellow enthusiasts. You’ll be surrounded by 3,000 show cars, 100,000+ spectators, and the unmistakable energy of race weekend—vintage race cars charging through the park just steps away, crowds lining the course, and a setting unlike anything else in the country.
This is not a foreign sports car show. This is a celebration of performance, heritage, and passion—where Pontiac’s legacy belongs front and center. Whether you’re preserving a concours original or driving a street-built muscle icon, you’ll find your place here.
Join us as we honor 100 years of Pontiac and Oakland in a way that only the PVGP can deliver—on the streets, on the grass, and in front of one of the most enthusiastic crowds in motorsports.
* * *
#### ****Pontiac Spotlight Show at Schenley Park – July 18/19 Weekend
The Pontiac Spotlight Car Show is on the Bob O’Connor Golf Course across the street from the clubhouse. Park your Pontiac on the golf course in the middle of the International Car Show – registration is for the entire weekend. Cost: $70 donation per car. The area is large enough to accommodate any and all Pontiacs. **REGISTER YOUR PONTIAC HERE**
**Your $70 Entry Donation includes:**
  * Weekend Parking spot on the golf course all weekend.
  * Weekend pass for driver and all passengers
  * Pontiacs and Oaklands of all years and models are welcome.
  * PVGP Race Program and sticker.


* * *
##### ****
####  Grand Prix Garden Party at Phipps Conservatory – Thursday, July 16
The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix planted the seeds for a fabulous new event in Schenley Park at the Phipps Conservatory & Botanical Gardens alongside the racetrack. The party showcases a variety of cars. This Garden Party features palate-pleasing food stations, wine, Helltown Beer and bar cocktails throughout one of the nation’s oldest and largest Victorian greenhouses. It promises to be an elegant and entertaining evening. 
With Pontiac as our Spotlight Car, we are seeking historically significant Pontiacs to display on the front lawn at the Garden Party. If you own a historically significant Pontiac, please send a photo and a brief description to Bob Speer for consideration by our committee for the special display in front of Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens. A second dedicated parking area will also be available for the other Pontiacs, which can be displayed together during the event.
Tickets are $295 per person. **DETAILS**
* * *
#### **  
******Tune-Up at the SouthSide Works – Wednesday, July 15
The PVGP Tune-Up was started in 2006 and has become a highlight of our Race Week Car Shows. Participation in this year’s Tune-Up Party is just $50. You get a reserved parking spot within the Automotive Showcase on the streets of the SouthSide Works. With Pontiac and Oakland as our Spotlight Car they will all be parked together. You will receive a car decal. Also included are two drink coupons for the driver, redeemable at any drink station. You can also register any guests for $25 each, and they will receive two complimentary drink coupons. **DETAILS**
* * *
####  Sewickley Stampede – Tuesday, July 14
Get ready for the Sewickley Stampede and RoundUp. It’s a street block party with race and exotic cars. Join us for an exclusive RoundUp at The Hotel and Rosa’s Cantina hosted by Robin Fernandez that will have you “Hootin’ and Hollerin’” for more.
The night begins with a RevLimiting, Rip Roarin’ Stampede Parade of Cars through the downtown business district of Sewickley, followed by the ‘Wrangling and Staging’ of cars in front of the hotel. Grab your best Pardner and come out to take in all the magnificent cars on the street, or purchase admission to the exclusive private party in The Hotel, featuring a light food menu, a cash bar, and live music.
The party begins at 6:00 PM at the Hotel and Rosa’s Cantina at 509 Beaver Street in Sewickley. **DETAILS**
* * *
#### Waterfront Car Cruise – Tuesday, July 14
Pontiac takes the spotlight early at the Waterfront Car Cruise, offering fans a first look at the 100th Anniversary celebration before it moves to Schenley Park. Held Tuesday, July 14 from 4:00–9:00 pm at the Waterfront in Homestead, this lively, open-to-all cruise brings together hundreds of classic and modern vehicles for a summer evening along the Monongahela.
No registration is required—just a $10 donation supports PVGP’s autism charities. With great food, vendors, and a strong showing of Pontiac and Oakland vehicles, the Cruise sets the tone for Race Week and is a must-attend stop for enthusiasts. **DETAILS**
* * *
#### PVGP Kick-Off Rallye – Sunday, July 12
If you like cars and country roads, this is a great way to spend a summer Sunday in your Pontiac. The Rallye is a driving tour and a scavenger hunt rolled into one. This is a casual and fun event with no experience required.
Your $80 entry includes participation in the Rallye for driver and navigator. We’re starting and concluding in Houston, PA, at Dual Devils Garage. Includes a deluxe cookout dinner and a great seasonal rotation of 17 Helltown Taproom craft beers. Tour their car exhibits and check out upcoming auction cars in their showroom. If we get more than 3 Pontiac entries, we will have a special award for the highest finisher. **DETAILS**
* * *
#### Blacktie & Tailpipes at Kamin Science Center – Saturday, July 11
Our Blacktie & Tailpipes Gala opens Grand Prix Race Week in formal style! This is a must for any auto enthusiast who enjoys shiny cars, fine dining and great company. In addition to being one of the city’s best summer parties, it is also a significant fundraiser for our charity partners.
We are excited to announce that the gala will be held at the Kamin Science Center on the North Shore. The PVGP will have access to the entire facility, and the new chair, Ev Kelly Searle, is planning a fabulous event. **DETAILS**

# Sewickley Stampede & Roundup
Tuesday, July 13, 2027
Get ready for the Sewickley Stampede and RoundUp. It’s a street block party with race and exotic cars. Join us for an exclusive RoundUp at The Hotel and Rosa’s Cantina that will have you Hootin’ and Hollerin’” for more.
The night begins with a RevLimiting, Stampede Parade of Cars through the downtown business district of Sewickley, followed by the ‘Wrangling and Staging’ of cars in front of the hotel.
Grab your best Pardner and come out to take in all the magnificent cars on the street, or purchase admission to the exclusive private party in The Hotel, featuring a light food menu and cash bar. Cost is $60 per person.
The party begins at 6:00 PM at the Hotel and Rosa’s Cantina at 509 Beaver Street in Sewickley. Like all Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix events, the proceeds benefit individuals with autism and intellectual/developmental disabilities.
* * *
#### Thank You to Our Generous Sponsors
#### Sewickley
The PVGP is very excited to bring our Motorsport Festival to Sewickley. When it comes to charm, Sewickley has it, from its bustling “village” of a business district to a range of terrific amenities, all within walking distance. Situated 11 miles northeast of downtown, on the Ohio River, this quaint borough of tree-lined streets with sidewalks is bordered by the neighboring boroughs of Edgeworth, Glen Osborne, and, on the hill overlooking town, Sewickley Heights.
* * *
#### History
Get ready to celebrate the spirit of the PVGP Tune-Up Party — and give a huge shoutout to the visionaries behind it all: Dotti and John Bechtol, and Rosemary and Joe Mendel! Back in 2006, they kicked off the very first Tune-Up at Bossa Nova restaurant downtown, gathering 75 guests and showcasing a dozen jaw-dropping cars. What started as a small, exclusive evening has shifted into a must-attend event, featuring hundreds of incredible vehicles, over 500 passionate participants, and an electric atmosphere of car lovers and spectators. Dan Holmes is taking the reins in 2026.
* * *
#### The Hotel & Rosa’s Cantina
Celebrate American History at the most legendary place in town, the Hotel & Rosa’s Cantina with a tasteful nod to the American West.
From savory homemade soups to specially blended brisket burgers and fresh salads, _the Hotel_ treats customers to the American comfort food we’ve all come to know and love. _The Hotel_ offers a little taste of Americana in a comfortable Western setting. At the same time, our outdoor dining area, Rosa’s Cantina Kitchen _,_ serves up a host of Tex-Mex favorites, including quesadillas, tacos, and fajitas. You are invited to this saloon setting for fresh and enjoyable comfort food, hand-crafted cocktails, and a wonderful selection of beers, bourbons, and tequila.
**_Giddy up!_**
#### Contact
Dan Holmes

# BMW Car Show and Club Gathering
**The PVGP and BMW CCA Allegheny Chapter are excited to host BMW as the 2027 Marque of the Year! Adding to the excitement, the BMW CCA will be bringing its O’Fest gathering to Pittsburgh. And to top it off, the BMW Classic Car Club of America will be making the PVGP its focus event for 2027. This promises to be an incredible week for all car enthusiasts! A full schedule of MOY and O’Fest events will be announced in the coming months, but save the date on your calendar: July 10-18, 2027! YOU’VE GOT TO BE HERE!**
The BMW Car Club of America’s Allegheny Chapter has long been one of the most passionate and impactful participants in the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, bringing an unmistakable energy and presence to German Hill each July. Known for their warm hospitality and innovative programming, the club has also set the benchmark for Marque of the Year fundraising – highlighted by a record-setting $126,500 contribution in 2018 and more than $425,000 raised in support of PVGP charities. Building on this remarkable legacy, we are proud to announce that BMW will return to the spotlight as our featured Marque of the Year in 2027, promising an even greater celebration of the Ultimate Driving Machine and the enthusiasts who make this community so special.
### 2026 BMW Activities
#####  Scenic Tour to Foxburg – Friday, July 17
The Friday Scenic Drive will take us from Fox Chapel, PA, and we’ll travel north and east of Pittsburgh on country roads to the breathtaking view at Brady’s Bend Overlook in Rimersburg. From there, we’ll make our way to our group lunch at Allegheny Grille in Foxburg, PA, with our dining room overlooking the Allegheny River. The Registration Fee is $20 per car. Registration does not include lunch. The drive will be limited to 25 cars. Route details to follow.
##### BMW Club Welcome Reception Dinner – Friday, July 17 6:30 – 8:00 PM
The Allegheny Chapter is happy to announce arrangements for our traditional Friday Evening Welcome Reception. Join them for Pizza and Wings on the rooftop deck of the Hotel Indigo. We like to welcome our guests by sharing distinctly Pittsburgh experiences. If you are from the ‘Burgh and the Squirrel Hill neighborhood in particular, one question you may have been asked is which do you like better: Mineo’s or Aiello’s. Both pizza houses have long-standing Pittsburgh histories. They will order Pizza and Wings from both houses and let you decide which is best! As is our tradition, the hotel will provide a cash bar, but the first drink is on the Chapter! We should also have a few door prizes. We ask for a $25 registration fee to attend the event. Proceeds benefit the PVGP charities.
##### Schenley Park Race Weekend – July 18-19
With the announced opening of the Panther Hollow Bridge, we are excited to welcome back the full course, complete with racing BMWs. Join the region’s premier car show at the BMW Club’s Schenley Park Car Corral, featuring a special celebration of the iconic BMW E30 M3. With wheel-to-wheel racing once again charging past the tent, there’s no better place to experience the action. Your registration includes weekend parking in the Car Corral, access to the BMW hospitality tent, a race program, and a commemorative decal. Known for its welcoming atmosphere, the BMW Club tent at Turn 13 is one of the best vantage points on the course.
All BMW years and models are welcome.
##### Registration to Open in 2027
Online registration closes at midnight on July 15. After that, registration is available only at the gate, and the fee increases by $10. Your registration is a charitable donation that supports the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix and our beneficiary charities. Because registration fees directly support our charitable mission and event operations, they are non-refundable. Thank you for your generosity and support.
##### Hotel Partner
The Indigo Hotel, located at 329 Technology Drive, Pittsburgh, PA 15219, is the official hotel partner of the BMW Club. There is a group rate of $165 a night plus $10 for special parking for your BMW.  
**Book your Room Online**
#### Allegheny Chapter BMW CCA
The Allegheny Chapter BMW CCA is a long-time supporter of the PVGP. The Chapter takes pride in its fundraising efforts as well as bringing innovation and excitement to its annual activities at the PVGP.
BMW magazine Roundel editor Satch Carlson visited the PVGP in 2015 and a glowing review for our old city. Satch is also a columnist for Hemmings Sports & Exotic Car, and well known as a former columnist for AutoWeek
Allegheny Chapter events are open to all years and models of the marque. The club hosts tours, social gatherings, and autocross. If you have an interest in joining, please stop by the tent or visit the club online at alleghenybmwcca.org.
In January of 2016, the Allegheny Chapter was recognized as the 2015 International Club of the Year Award. Congratulations,, the award is well deserved!
Join the biggest car show in the region at the BMW Club’s Schenley Park Car Corral. The club has a reputation for its warm hospitality and many believe that the BMW tent at Schenley Park is the best place to watch the races as the racers enter the golf course after sprinting up the hill to turn #13. You do not have to be a member of BMW CCA to take part in the activities in Schenley Park! As always, all years and models of BMWs are welcome!.
Many thanks to BMWCCA, both the national organization and the local Allegheny Chapter for hosting an incredible O’Fest during the 2018 Grand Prix. There were Bimmers everywhere during the week and over 750 at Schenley Park. The club set the all-time record for Marque fundraising with a $126,500 donation! Together with the Pittsburgh BMW dealers and the national BMW CCA, the Allegheny Club Chapter has raised an astounding $425,000 for the Grand Prix charities!
The Club’s mission is to promote the interest in, the ownership of, and preservation of classic BMWs, as well as to encourage their use and visibility. They do this mainly through the organization of and the participation in specific events, and the publication of a quarterly magazine THE ULTIMATE CLASSIC. They are in contact with other BMW clubs in order to keep members abreast of events and happenings in the US as well as abroad. A strong emphasis is being placed on social contacts between members. The Club also maintains a register of members and their cars.
Honorary Race Director and BMW racer Bill Auberlen takes his BMW Z4 GTLM around the track on an exhibition lap at Schenley Park in 2018.
**Special Volunteers: Mike Renner and his BMW Ring Taxi**
Ever wondered what it’s like to experience the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix from inside the snow fence beside the action?
Each year, Mike Renner delivers that thrill with the BMW Ring Taxi – one of the most popular attractions at Schenley Park.
Inspired by the legendary Sabine Schmitz and her high-speed passenger laps at the Nürburgring, the BMW CCA Allegheny Chapter brought the Ring Taxi concept to the PVGP in 2009. Mike, an instructor from the BMW Performance Center, volunteered – and the response was immediate.
Since then, Mike has returned every year, giving charity laps in the latest BMW performance cars and occasionally pre-production models. His runs, often during lunch and between race groups, have become a must-see (and must-ride) experience.
Just as important, Mike continues to support the PVGP’s mission by donating BMW Performance Center driving schools and auction items, helping raise thousands of dollars annually for our charity partners.
A skilled racer and instructor, Mike makes it look dramatic – especially sliding through Turn 13 – but he’s always in control. More than that, he’s embraced the spirit of the PVGP, sharing his passion with fans and representing the event wherever he goes.
If you get the chance to ride along, take it. It’s one of the most unforgettable experiences of the weekend.
Mike takes the Ring Taxi into a turn at Schenley Park
The PVGP is one of Mike’s favorite events. He said: “I love coming to the PVGP because of the unique nature of the event. The city does such a great job making the event happen. Everyone involved is incredibly friendly and welcoming. The PVGP organizers do a great job of making things fun and unique, and the Allegheny Chapter does a great job with its corral.”
Due to the tremendous capabilities of the new BMW M cars, Mike is able to give a thrilling but safe ride to those lucky enough to get a seat in his car. Everyone who gets out after a lap has an ear-to-ear grin. This year the club is asking $50 per seat for a ride with Mike. To learn more about how you too can experience the PVGP from the other side of the fence and possibly enjoy the best ride in the park, head to the BMW tent on German Hill, come to Turn 15 at lunchtime Saturday where Charity Rides are staged, or stop in at the MINI Track Rides Tent at the top of Serpentine Drive.
We thank Mike for being such a wonderful ambassador for BMW, the BMW CCA, and most importantly, the PVGP.

# Vintage Motorbike Show
##### **Weekend July 17-18, 2027**
Motorbikes of all historic, vintage, and antique brands are welcome to join in and strut their stuff. Bring on the Italians, Americans, Brits, Asians, Germans, and more.
Since 2012 motorbike friends, collectors and enthusiasts have met on the hill above the serpentine of Pittsburgh’s Schenley Park during the annual Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix. Take in the vintage races and car shows from one of the best vantage points in the park under the cool shade of the trees.
In keeping with the spirit of the PVGP, all classic, vintage, antique, and historic racing motorbikes are invited to participate in the show which runs from 9:30 am until 5:00 pm Saturday and Sunday.
##### Registration to Open in 2027
Your $25 fee includes your weekend car display spot and a PVGP decal. You will receive a PVGP wristband ($20 value) that provides access to the show field at the start/finish area. Includes an exclusive motorcycle entrance to the park and all-day parking.
  * Gates open at 7:00 AM.
  * $25 for the weekend
  * $15 for single day
  * $10 for additional wristbands


#####  Contact
The Ton-Up Pittsburgh manages the PVGP’s, Motorbike Show. They are vintage motorcycle enthusiasts with a passion for primarily British bikes, Rockabilly, and the Rockers subculture. The PVGP is excited to have them on the team and looks forward to another great year.
Please contact  
Patrick Martin 412 584-9359  
or  
Sergio Kyriakis 412 443-6979
Visit the Motorbike Facebook page or the Ton-Up Pittsburgh Facebook page
**Gear Up for Your Next Adventure from Viking Bags!**
Whether you’re heading to the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix or hitting the open road, the Viking Voyage Large Motorcycle Backpack delivers versatility and convenience. With 30 liters of storage, weather-resistant Cordura construction, a padded laptop sleeve and multiple compartments, it keeps your essentials organized. Wear it as a backpack or secure it to your motorcycle’s sissy bar. Built for riders who appreciate performance and practicality, it’s a great companion for your next journey!
Viking has supported the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix since 2021, donating products for us to raffle for charity. **Viking Bags Website**
##### All Motorcycles are Welcome
Day of show registration is available. please enter from Darlington Road.
There is **no overnight camping** available and limited trailer parking – please inquire.
The show takes place on the corner of the golf course along Darlington Road and East Circuit Road. See the map below. Please enter from Squirrel Hill into East Circuit and directly into the park. You can preregister or pay at the gate. A PVGP vendor will be nearby all weekend selling food and drinks.
_**We want to thank Tip Paul and the Moto Guzzi Club for establishing the PVGP Vintage Motorbike Show and growing it into a thriving event. Tip is stepping down as the director of the event after 5 years but he promises to be there with his bikes…he deserves a chance to sit back and enjoy what he has helped create.**_

# PVGP Association
The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix is quite a unique vintage racing event. With 10 days of races, car shows and parties it is one of our country’s largest vintage races, and the only one run through actual city streets – the way sports car racing began in the 40s and 50s.
Our mission is to celebrate and honor our founding auto enthusiasts while simultaneously benefiting charity. Funds raised provide residential care, treatment and support for individuals with autism and intellectual/developmental disabilities in western Pennsylvania
We want to thank our army of volunteers who work all year to make the races and shows run successfully.

# Trailer Parking
## Trailer Parking for Car Show Participants – July 17/18, 2027
The growth of our International Car Show at Schenley Park has helped elevate our event to new heights, but with 3,000 show cars, there is no space on the golf course to park trailers and tow vehicles. Schenley Park is in a tightly congested area with limited parking options, so if you decide to bring your car on a trailer, you have limited options during the event:
**Option 1: Flagstaff Hill Parking  
** You must pay $50 daily to park your trailer and tow vehicle on Flagstaff Hill. This is the large, gently sloping grass hill across the street from Phipps Conservatory—see image below. You must enter from Schenley Drive after crossing the bridge from Schenley Plaza. We suggest using Phipps Conservatory as the GPS location. Once you have paid and parked, you can unload your car and drive it up to the golf course. Details on Flagstaff Hill Parking.
**Option 2: Surface Parking Lots  
** Limited parking lots in Oakland accommodate a trailer with a tow vehicle.
**Flagstaff Hill Parking is shown in the middle of the image. Phipps Conservatory is at the bottom.**
**Free Shuttle Bus Route Map – transports you to the Car Show on the Bob O’Connor Golf Course at Schenley Park.**

# Kick-Off Rallye
Sunday, July 12, 2026
**2026 RALLYE RESULTS**
**2025 RALLYE RESULTS**
The PVGP is already gearing up for our Kick-Off Rallye at Dual Devils Garage in 2026. The date has been moved to Sunday, July 12, just one week before Schenley Park.Our Rallymaster is planning a route through the back roads of Washington County.
Our Kick-Off Rallye is truly the kick-off event of the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, as it occurs one week before our Race Week. The competition consists of a combined Monte Carlo/Gimmick rally requiring no prior experience. You can compete in any vehicle you like – any year, any make – no restrictions. We welcome unique and different cars. With Jaguar as the Marque and Pontiac as the Spotlight, we expect a large contingent of each – special prizes will be awarded.

**The PVGP welcomes Northwest Bank as a partner for 2026**  
Northwest Bank is a valued community partner whose commitment to the regions it serves aligns closely with the mission of the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix. With deep local roots, the bank actively invests in the well-being of its communities through charitable giving, volunteerism, and financial education initiatives. Their support of programs focused on affordable housing, education, and neighborhood development reflects a genuine dedication to helping individuals and families thrive. Northwest Bank’s focus on community impact makes them a natural fit for the PVGP, where giving back and supporting local charities are at the heart of everything we do.

##### Schedule – July 12, 2026
Registration: 9:30 – 11:00 am  
Mandatory Drivers Meeting: 11:00– 11:15 am  
Rallye Cars Start Departing: 11:30 am (one leaves every minute)  
Meals are served as you return, starting at 2:00 pm  
Awards: 4:30 pm
Any car enthusiast can register for a fun but competitive mystery course to test their driving, navigational and trivia skills through the Pittsburgh countryside. Paul MacIntyre and Chuck Larouere are already planning new twists for this year.
##### What is a Rallye?
You don’t have to be a racer or have experience in a rally competition to enjoy our Kick-Off Rallye. Each year it helps us kick off the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix. Any car enthusiast can register for a fun but competitive mystery course that will test your driving, navigational and trivia skills through the western PA countryside.
Chuck Larouere returned as Rallyemaster in 2021 and brought the latest technology. We utilized Richta Rally so all competitors can download the app for free and it automatically acknowledges as you pass the electronic checkpoints. No volunteers are required on the course and it’s all touchless! You will know your score and standing while you drive! Now, everyone can enjoy participating in the rally, as no checkpoint crews are required. Just like magic!
##### Contact
For details, email Paul MacIntyre

# Countryside Tour
Thursday, July 16, 2026
Flickr Gallery for Countryside Tour – Click the image above to view the entire album
If driving your classic sports car is your main passion, we invite you to join us for the Countryside Tour. Participation is limited to sports & GT cars produced in 1983 and earlier*
Bud Osbourne conceived the Countryside Tour in 2012 as part of the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix. Bud has handed over the reins to Derek Kuntz and Marla Taylor-Kuntz.
The tour follows a delightful collection of scenic, twisting, lightly traveled back roads through Pennsylvania’s beautiful Laurel Highlands. Be advised that this is a DRIVING tour and not for the faint of heart. We cover many miles, and it’s all back roads at a brisk pace!
**Schedule – Thursday, July 16, 2026**  
First Group Starts: 9:00 AM from Liberty Pole Spirits  
Lunch at Jamison Farm: 1:00 – 2:30 PM
The 2026 Countryside Tour will kick off from Liberty Pole Spirits in Washington, PA (800 Adios Drive Washington, PA 15301). Registration will begin at 8:00am. There are many hotels in the area if you chose to stay the night before the tour; Hyatt Place at The Hollywood Casino, DoubleTree by Hilton Washington Meadow Lands Casino, Hampton Inn & Suites Pittsburgh-Meadow Lands, Courtyard by Marriott Pittsburgh Washington/Meadow Lands, Holiday Inn Express & Suites Washington-Meadow Lands, WoodSpring Suites Washington Meadowlands PA, Fairfield by Marriott Inn & Suites Washington Casino.
* * *
**Registration Open  
**
Registration is $85.00 and includes both morning and afternoon tour segments, as well as lunch and refreshments for two people at Jamison Farm. Extra lunches are $35 each.
**Contact**
If you have any questions, please contact  
**_Derek Kuntz_**  
_**Marla Taylor-Kuntz**_
* * *
We are proud to welcome SanaView Farms Winery as a valued partner of the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix Countryside Tour. Nestled in the scenic Laurel Highlands, this historic 52-acre farm and boutique winery is known for its exceptional small-batch natural wines and memorable farm-to-table experiences. SanaView Farms Winery will be sharing their fine wines at a variety of PVGP events throughout the year, including the Countryside Tour, adding a distinctive local flavor to the festivities. We’re delighted to have them join the PVGP family and invite you to enjoy a taste of their remarkable wines this season.
**Lunch at Jamison Farm  
**On Tour Day, traveling in groups of three or four cars to enhance both safety and the driving experience, we will build a good thirst and an appetite, which will be slaked during our visit to Jamison Farm on another country road near Crabtree, PA. Owners John and Sukey Jamison continue to raise lambs and serve meals on-site, and they are excited to be our luncheon hosts this year. John is also a British car enthusiast and has been a Countryside Tour participant for many years.
A very talented cook, Sukey Jamison has created a line of hand-prepared lamb dishes, including a Lamb Stew created in collaboration with the late, great Jean-Louis Palladin and Sukey’s award-winning Lamb Pie.
After one of our Countryside Tours, a participant was heard to remark: “This is sort of like driving the Tail of the Dragon, only a lot longer and more fun.” We would have to add: “And a lot less crowded!” Whatever you do, please don’t delay in registering, as we are limited to roughly 50 cars and those “slots” fill up pretty quickly.
*In the case of air-cooled Porsche 911s, Alfa Romeo Spiders and a few others, cars newer than 1983 are accepted because they are a continuation of the original design.

# Mercedes-Benz Car Show
##### Weekend, July 17/18, 2027
Mark Sheldon, a longtime and active member of the Mercedes-Benz Club and a familiar face at the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, was seriously injured while volunteering during this year’s PVGP. Mark has given generously of his time and energy to our automotive community, and now he and his family could use our support. Please consider making a donation to help with the expenses associated with his recovery and rehabilitation.
For generations, the Mercedes-Benz Club of America Pittsburgh Section has been a passionate supporter of the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix and its charitable mission. Mercedes-Benz enthusiasts are invited to join us for an impressive display celebrating the elegance, engineering, and performance that define the marque. From timeless classics to modern luxury and AMG performance models, this gathering showcases the rich heritage and enduring appeal of Mercedes-Benz.
Whether you are a longtime club member, a first-time participant, or simply a fan of the brand, you are welcome to be part of the experience. While membership in the Mercedes-Benz Club is encouraged, it is not required to participate. Come share your passion, connect with fellow enthusiasts, and enjoy one of the premier automotive weekends in the country.
##### Location
The Mercedes-Benz car show will be in their exciting trackside location in Schenley Park at turn 13.
##### Silver Star Preservation Class
The Mercedes-Benz Club of America Silver Star Preservation Class is a certification program designed specifically for vehicles that are 25 years or older, largely original, and unrestored since new. Check the box after you enter your cell phone number during registration if you want to enter your car.
#####  The MB Market
A special thank you to MB Market for sponsoring the Mercedes-Benz Club tent and for our participants at this year’s Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix. MB Market is an online marketplace dedicated exclusively to Mercedes-Benz vehicles, connecting enthusiasts, collectors and sellers through curated auctions of everything from classic models to modern performance cars. Their support helped make the Mercedes-Benz experience at Schenley Park even more special, and we greatly appreciate their commitment to the PVGP and the enthusiast community.
##### Registration to Open in 2027
Join the biggest car show in the region at the Mercedes-Benz Club’s Schenley Park Car Show. All Mercedes-Benz enthusiasts are invited to join the Mercedes-Benz Club Pittsburgh Section for a spectacular display of new and vintage Mercedes-Benz automobiles at this year’s Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix. Although club membership is suggested, you do not need to be a club member to participate, but we recommend joining this great group.
**Cost: $70 donation per car**
  * Includes weekend parking on the golf course with access to a trackside club tent.
  * Complimentary PVGP Race Program and decal.
  * Wristband for driver and one passenger, good for the weekend.
  * Online registration closes at midnight July 16 and you must pay at the gate after that.
  * Lunches are available to pre-purchase at $30 per person per day.


* * *
Mark Sheldon, a longtime and active member of the Mercedes-Benz Club and a familiar face at the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix, was seriously injured while volunteering during this year’s PVGP. Mark has given generously of his time and energy to our automotive community, and now he and his family could use our support. Please consider donating to help cover the expenses associated with his recovery and rehabilitation.
**All Mercedes-Benz enthusiasts are invited to join with the Mercedes-Benz Club Pittsburgh Section for a spectacular display of Mercedes-Benz automobiles at this year’s Grand Prix. Although club membership is suggested, you do not need to be a club member to participate.**
**The Mercedes-Benz area will display all years and types of Mercedes- Benz vehicles – from Concours quality to your everyday driver.**
##### Contact MBCA – Pittsburgh
The Pittsburgh Chapter of the Mercedes-Benz Club of America has been an active partner of the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix and hosts the tent at Schenley Park. The club hosts activities and events for all Mercedes-Benz enthusiasts including social events, car shows, and driving events. Please contact Dan Marcin with any questions.

# Grand Prix Garden Party at Phipps Conservatory
Thursday, July 16, 2026
* * *
This year’s event will feature a curated display of concours-quality automobiles on the front lawn of the Phipps Conservatory. Guests can expect a stunning selection of vehicles. With Jaguar as the Marque of the Year for the and the International Jaguar Festival taking place during PVGP Race Week, along with our Pontiac Spotlight, we are seeking historically significant Jaguars to display at the Garden Party. If you own a historically significant Jaguar, please send a photo and a brief description to Bob Speer for consideration by our committee for the special display in front of Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens. A second dedicated parking area will also be available for the other Jaguars which can be displayed together during the event.
Set within one of the nation’s oldest and grandest Victorian greenhouses, the evening will include hors d’oeuvres, flavorful food stations, and a full selection of wine, beer, and cocktails, served under elegant tents and throughout the gardens. It promises to be an unforgettable summer evening.
The party begins at 6:00 PM on the front lawn and in the Phipps Outdoor Garden with food, drinks, and live music. Guests are also invited to enjoy the natural beauty of the Conservatory throughout the evening.
****
This elegant evening marks the start of Schenley Park Race Weekend, offering guests an exclusive opportunity to enjoy a curated collection of classic automobiles against the stunning backdrop of one of the nation’s oldest and largest Victorian greenhouses.
UBS Walnut Wealth Management returns as the Presenting Partner of this special event. Their continued support underscores a shared commitment to excellence and community engagement.
As with every PVGP event, exceptional cars will take center stage. In addition to the featured display, Schenley Drive will offer reserved parking for select fine automobiles driven by our guests. Those not arriving in show cars are kindly asked to park on Flagstaff Hill. There is no charge for parking.
### About Phipps Conservatory
A beloved Pittsburgh landmark, Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens, was established in 1892 by philanthropist Henry W. Phipps as a gift to the city. The historic glasshouse serves as a dramatic backdrop to the Garden Party and the starting line for this year’s races.
Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens was built by philanthropist Henry W. Phipps in 1892 as a gift for the people of Pittsburgh. It towers over the starting line of our races.
* * *
* * *
### 
### Meet the Artist: Olga Taimanov
Garden Party guests will enjoy the elegant music of violinist Olga Taimanov, an accomplished performer whose career has taken her from international concert halls to stages throughout the United States.
A classically trained musician, Olga has performed with renowned orchestras and appeared alongside celebrated artists including Andrea Bocelli, The Three Tenors, Lady Gaga, and Christina Aguilera. Today, she brings her versatile repertoire to audiences throughout the region, performing both classical and contemporary music on traditional and electric violin.
Her artistry and engaging style provide the perfect accompaniment to an evening in the garden, creating a sophisticated and memorable atmosphere for one of Grand Prix week’s most special events.
Olga is excited to share that during the Garden Event she will be introducing her new signature British Music Collection: “From Beatles to Coldplay and Beyond ”- a musical journey throughout some of the United Kingdom’s most iconic artist and songs.
* * *

**The party begins at 6:00 PM in the Phipps Outdoor Garden, with food, drinks, and live music beginning at 6:30 PM.**
  * Single Tickets: $325 until July 1, $350 after July 1
  * A Dozen Tickets: $3,250 for 12 tickets ($271 each)

# Marque & Spotlight History
The Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix began the practice of honoring a specific car brand beginning with our third race back in 1985. Many of auto racing’s preeminent manufacturers have been recognized at our event.
French for “brand,” marque (pronounced “mark”) refers to a brand name given to a line of automobiles. For example, Mercedes-Benz is a marque, whereas the Mercedes-Benz 560SL is a make of the Mercedes-Benz marque. Industry consolidation has slightly clouded this designation, but marque is still used to define a particular line of vehicles. It is a term typically reserved, however, for the more prestigious motoring brands.
